Purpose

o Pick the fields you want to use in your calculation.

4. Add Operators
o Use the mathematical operators provided: +, -, *, /, parentheses ().

o Example formula for stock valuation:
o (Quantity in stock) * (Unit price)

▪ Open a parenthesis (
▪ Send Quantity in stock to the formula window

▪ Send Unit price to the formula window

▪ Close parenthesis )
6. Validate
o Click Validate to save and make the formula usable.

within SpeedWMS.

Carrier Allocation
Purpose
• Automatically assign the correct carrier to orders based on predefined rules
and conditions.
• Ensures efficient shipping and reduces manual allocation errors.
Access
• Menu path: Settings / Transport / Carrier Allocation
Key Components
1. Sequences Tab (Default View)
o Displays the list of sequences for carrier assignment.
o A sequence is a set of conditions that, when met, automatically
assigns a specific carrier to an order.
2. Columns Tab
o Only headings (fields) that are activated in the Columns tab can be
used to define conditions.
o Example fields: customer, order type, delivery location, etc.
3. Creating Sequences
o Use the Add button or contextual menu to create a new sequence.
o Define conditions based on the selected columns.
o Partial conditions are allowed: not all fields need to be filled.
4. Modifying & Reordering Sequences
o Sequences can be edited or reordered using the arrows in the upperright corner.
o Order matters: sequences are evaluated from top to bottom; the first
matching sequence assigns the carrier.
5. Direct Carrier Assignment from Orders
o Carrier can also be assigned manually directly from the Orders
window, if needed.
Sensitivity: Internal

Usage Notes
• Always ensure the relevant columns are activated before creating
sequences.
• Proper sequence order ensures priority rules are respected.
• This feature can save time for warehouses handling multiple carriers and
complex delivery rules.

Creation of Receipt Lines
Purpose
• After generating the receipt header, individual receipt lines must be added.
• Each line corresponds to a storage medium to be put into stock.
• Receipt lines capture: item code, quantity, quality, and any traceability
information if required.
Mandatory Information for Each Line
1. Item code – must exist in SpeedWMS; cannot receive unregistered items.
2. Quantity – always expressed in units per storage medium.
3. Quality – default quality comes from the item sheet or activity default.
4. Traceability info – required if the item is configured for traceability (lot, DLC,
DLUO, etc.).
5. Owner – automatically populated if defined on item or activity; can be
manually selected from allowed third parties.
Methods to Add Receipt Lines
1. Direct Addition
• Enter item code, quantity, and quality directly in the code field.
2. Search by Item Code
• Right-click the code field → Search for an article.
• Can display items attached to the supplier or all items using “All Suppliers”.
• Select the item → automatically fills the code field; enter quantity and
quality.
3. Add via Grid Pattern
• Access item templates registered in the activity from the code field
contextual menu.
• Enter quantities:
o All column → same quantity for all items sharing a main characteristic.
Sensitivity: Internal

o Individual column → quantity per specific reference.
• Validated quantities generate receipt lines displayed in the receipt window.
4. Detailed Entry Form
• Double-click the code field → opens detailed entry form.
• Allows filling all available fields for a receipt line.
• Supports multiple logistic variants and traceability fields if configured.
• Useful for complex items requiring lot/batch tracking.
5. Import via Excel
• Excel file must have 3 columns: item code, quantity, quality code.
• Features:
o Unknown item code column flags items not existing in Speed.
o Import first line toggle for headers.
o Preview shows data as it will be imported.
• Validation → creates receipt lines automatically.
• Can modify the receiving dock or update previously entered lines during
import.
Important Notes
• Added lines are not immediately in stock; stock generation must be
performed separately.
• Receipt lines can be modified or deleted via contextual menu before stock
generation without affecting system history.
• If associated with expected items, consumption is not recorded until stock
entry movement occurs.
• Supports bulk entry with splitting over multiple storage media if required.

SpeedWMS – Location Search
Access:
• Menu: Settings → Locations → Location Search
Purpose:
• Suggests the optimal destination location for each stock medium.
• Uses predefined rules and criteria to guide operators to the correct storage
slot.
Available Actions:
• Create new location search rules.
• Modify existing rules.
• Delete rules (with constraints).
Multiple location search rules can exist for the same activity.
Rule Structure:
• Each location search rule is made of sequences.
• Each sequence has a method:
1. Search location in structure
o Finds the first empty slot in a storage area.
2. Search as close as possible to picking
o Finds the first empty slot near the picking location of the item.
3. Search by complement
o Finds a location already occupied by the same item reference.
4. Fixed search
o Returns a predetermined fixed location.
5. Free search
o Custom method for specific needs; configurable only by BK Systems
teams.
Sensitivity: Internal

Each method can be refined with criteria such as classification, size, quality, or
weight. Multiple methods can be combined within a single rule, and multiple
sequences of the same method can exist within a rule.
Sequence Execution Logic:
• Sequences are executed in the order defined within the rule.
• Possible outcomes for each sequence:
1. No location found → Move to next sequence (or end search if none
remain).
2. Location found → Proposed to the operator; end of search.
Best practice: Configure sequences to perform the most precise searches first,
with broader searches in later sequences.
Usage:
• Location search rules can be linked to Speed item sheets, ensuring the
system proposes the best location based on the item characteristics and
warehouse rules.
Sensitivity: Internal

SpeedWMS – Reception Principle
Purpose:

A. Portfolio of Expected Items

orders.

o Manually by the user, or
o Automatically via an interface from an external system (e.g., N+1
sales management system).
• At the end of the reception process, SpeedWMS allows the generation of a
comparative report between:
o Quantities expected and
o Quantities actually received.
B. Reception Module
• Receptions are carried out declaratively, based on the items physically
received.
• Receptions can be fed by an interface or processed via:
o Radio Frequency (RF) module, or
o Manual entry.
2. Key Notes
• The choice of method depends on the business process and whether prenotification of arrivals is available.
• Comparative reporting in expected items ensures accurate tracking and
stock reconciliation.

I. Summary
• Goal: Automatically replenish picking locations (ZPA) in multiples of VL cartons, filling to
the location volume (location volume vs. article volume × quantity).
• Net requirement calculation: portfolio requirements in units – available ZPA stock – ZPA
replenishment pending (real quantities).
• Operator optimization: chain missions from the same origin support via support scan.
II. Context & Scope
• Dynamic picking replenishment happens in SPEED via the ZPA transfer.
• Standard system limitations require multiple RF steps for operational needs. The goal is
to make dynamic location replenishment more efficient by fully automating the process.
Sensitivity: Internal

• This process is distinct from wave launches but is driven by the order portfolio.
Scope:
• ZPA dynamic replenishment in multiples of VL cartons from reserve to dynamic picking
locations.
• Priority: same article/lot.
• Execution of replenishment mission.
Target steps (hypotheses):
1. ZPA placement rule (find location by volume + deduct quantities from previous steps).
2. Picking replenishment module – optimize chaining of replenishments from the same
origin location.
III. Definitions & Parameters
Term Description
VL pallet (PCB palette) Units per full pallet (e.g., 100)
VL carton (PCB carton) Units per carton (configurable)
Unit volume (VU) cm³ per unit (configurable per article)
Location capacity Maximum volume in cm³ (configurable)
Replenishment rounding rule Minimum = VL carton; always multiples of VL carton
Mixing lots in dynamic picking Not allowed by default
Swelling coefficient Allows placement even if within ±X% of location volume
IV. Current Issue
• WMS proposes transferring the full original support to the dynamic picking location.
• If support volume exceeds location capacity → operator manually enters partial quantity
to complete replenishment, then splits the original support and stores remnants
manually elsewhere.
Sensitivity: Internal

• No multi-location guidance, no consideration of subsequent manual placement
destinations.
Consequences:
• RF overload, error risks, wasted time, stock inconsistencies.
V. Target Solution
• Net requirement calculation (per article/lot): Needs – ZPA available – pending ZPA
replenishment.
Example:
Order Cmd1 Cmd2 Cmd3 Total
Raw need (article A) 10 102 33 145
Picking units (raw) 10 2 33 45
ZPA unallocated stock 0 0 0 0
Pending ZPA replenishment 0 0 0 0
Net picking need 45
• Round net need to VL carton: 45 → 50
• Target search: first fill existing ZPA locations (same article/lot) to volume, in multiples of
VL carton. If capacity < VL carton → skip and open new locations per placement rules.
Stepwise example:
Step Location Available volume Possible cartons Proposed Deposited qty Remaining
0 — — — — 0 50
1 E1 96000 2.133 2 20 30
2 E2 96000 2.133 2 20 10
3 E3 96000 2.133 2 10 0
• Mission chaining: create 3 missions linked to same origin support with replenishment
qty 20/20/5 → target locations E1, E2, E3.
Sensitivity: Internal

• Reservations & consistency: consider these missions in next ZPA transfers.
Second launch example:
Order Cmd4 Cmd2 Cmd3 Total
Raw need (article A) 25 102 33 160
Picking units (raw) 25 2 33 60
ZPA unallocated stock 30 — — —
Pending ZPA replenishment 5 — — —
Net picking need 25
• Round net need: 25 → 30
Stepwise example 2:
Step Location Available volume Possible cartons Proposed Deposited qty Remaining
0 — — — — 0 30
1 E3 51000 1.133 1 10 20
2 E6 96000 2.133 2 20 0
• Consider pending missions even if not yet executed.
VI. Business Rules
• Must be multiples of VL cartons; never single units.
• Strict capacity respect (volume) including swelling coefficient.
• Priority: existing picking locations (same article/lot). No lot mixing.
• Origin support selection: FEFO, DAEN, sufficient quantity.
• Key parameters: location volume, unit volume, VL carton volume, swelling coefficient.
VII. RF Ergonomics
Sensitivity: Internal

Option 1:
• Scan origin support → display ZPA route (location 1…X & quantities).
• Guided to each target → deposit calculated qty → validation.
• Random adaptation: allow lower quantity.
• End of route: return to mission list. Remaining qty stays in reserve location.
Option 2:
• Scan origin → retrieve mission 1
• Go to target 1 → deposit qty → validation
• Automatically continue to mission 2 using same origin location
• Deposit qty → validation
• End of route → return to mission list, leftover stays in reserve
Option 3:
• Scan origin → retrieve mission 1
• Go to target 1 → deposit qty → validation
• Return to mission list
• Allow scan of support to enter mission instead of location (avoids going back to location)
• Deposit qty → validation
• Return to mission list
VIII. Points of Attention
• Deduct pending replenishments in real quantities (not origin support capacity).
• Replenish in multiples of cartons; ZPA transfer already in VL carton multiples → check
parameterization and impact.
• Lot mixing not allowed by default.

SECTION 1 — Business Context

Within the L’Oréal project, several location search rules are defined to meet
storage constraints.
These rules are based on article classification criteria.
The client now wants to configure a Free Location Search rule that:

1.2 Objective of the Rule
The rule must:
1. Count the number of locations containing the same article within a given
zone.
2. Compare that count to the article’s dynamic picking threshold
(ART_ALPHA10).
3. Apply the following logic:
Case 1 — Location Count < Threshold
→ Assign a new free location in the defined zone.
Case 2 — Location Count ≥ Threshold
→ Do not propose a new location.
→ Move to the next storage sequence (e.g., reserve storage).

1.0 Initial Version 14/04/2023 AKD
BUSINESS CONTEXT
4.1 Business Requirement
Within the L’ORÉAL activity, the client requires that:
When closing a reception,
If there are still pending expected lines (not received) linked to the current reception
DO reference,
These pending lines must be automatically settled (closed).
4.2 Why This Control Is Required
This control aims to:
Prevent reporting inconsistencies
• When a reception is closed, reception data is transmitted.
• The DO reference is closed.
• The same DO reference must NOT be receivable again in another reception.
Clean the reception backlog (expected lines portfolio)
• An expected line with the same BL reference as a closed reception can no
longer be processed by operators.
• The client would otherwise need to resend a new expected line.
4.3 Clarification Regarding DO References
Speed technically allows multiple DO references per reception.
However, for this activity:
One reception = One DO reference
Therefore:
Sensitivity: Internal

metadata.source: LOREAL Reception Closure – Automatic Settlement of Pending Expected Lines.txt
metadata.source_file: LOREAL Reception Closure – Automatic Settlement of Pending Expected Lines.txt

text:
The logic must use:
REE_NOFO = BL Reference (REA_BL)
The pending expected lines to settle must match:
• The DO reference of the reception
• The BL reference (REE_NOFO)
4.4 Radio Behavior
There will be:
No reception closure allowed from radio.
This option will be blocked.
Closure is handled only in Speed Admin.
CONFIGURATION PARAMETER
Parameter Description
ACT_TOP21 Enables or disables automatic settlement logic
If:
ACT_TOP21 = 1
→ Apply settlement logic.
If:
ACT_TOP21 = 0
→ Standard behavior (no automatic settlement).
TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION
6.1 Entry Point Used
Sensitivity: Internal

metadata.source: LOREAL Reception Closure – Automatic Settlement of Pending Expected Lines.txt
metadata.source_file: LOREAL Reception Closure – Automatic Settlement of Pending Expected Lines.txt

text:
Entry Point Description
PE22 Triggered after reception closure in Speed Admin
6.2 Functional Trigger
Trigger occurs:
When:
• A reception is selected
• User clicks the "Close" button
• Reception closure is completed
Then:
→ Execute additional logic via PE22.
6.3 PE22 – Pending Line Settlement Logic
Condition
IF ACT_TOP21 = 1
Then execute the following:
Step 1 – Verify Pending Lines
After reception closure:
Check if there are remaining expected lines (attendus):
• Linked to the same DO reference
• Matching BL reference (REE_NOFO = REA_BL)
• Not fully consumed
Step 2 – Behavior
Case 1 – No Remaining Expected Lines
Sensitivity: Internal

metadata.source: LOREAL Reception Closure – Automatic Settlement of Pending Expected Lines.txt
metadata.source_file: LOREAL Reception Closure – Automatic Settlement of Pending Expected Lines.txt

text:
If no pending expected lines exist:
→ Do nothing.
Case 2 – Remaining Expected Lines Exist
If pending expected lines remain:
→ Automatically settle (close) the remaining expected lines for that reception.
6.4 Logical Flow (Pseudo-code)
IF ACT_TOP21 = 1 THEN
reception_DO = CURRENT_RECEPTION_DO
reception_BL = REE_NOFO
pending_lines = GET_EXPECTED_LINES(
DO = reception_DO,
BL = reception_BL,
status = NOT_CONSUMED
)
IF pending_lines IS NOT EMPTY THEN
FOR each line IN pending_lines:
SET line.status = CLOSED
ENDFOR
ENDIF
ENDIF
Sensitivity: Internal

metadata.source: LOREAL Reception Closure – Automatic Settlement of Pending Expected Lines.txt
metadata.source_file: LOREAL Reception Closure – Automatic Settlement of Pending Expected Lines.txt

text:
FUNCTIONAL SUMMARY (RAG-Optimized)
What triggers this logic?
Reception closure in Speed Admin.
Is radio affected?
Yes – radio closure is blocked.
No settlement logic runs from radio.
Which parameter controls activation?
ACT_TOP21
Which entry point is used?
PE22
What is the matching key?
• DO reference
• BL reference (REE_NOFO = REA_BL)
What happens if pending expected lines remain?
They are automatically settled.
What happens if none remain?
Nothing.
TECHNICAL IMPACT
• No new tables created.
• No UI modification.
• Logic only executed at reception closure.
• Ensures data consistency.
• Prevents re-processing of closed DO references.
• Cleans reception backlog.

• Does not split intelligently based on capacity
This causes:
• Lack of shelf space
• Large variability in article volume (lipsticks vs bottles)
• No automatic calculation of remaining capacity
• Manual management of partial replenishments
SECTION 2 — Functional Objectives
The workshop defined the following goals:
1. Automatically split replenishments according to destination volume.
2. Fill picking locations based on volume, not only quantity.
3. Improve ergonomics in the replenishment module.
4. Make ZPA replenishment more dynamic (triggered at wave launch).
5. Manage saturated locations (rejection or deferred handling).
6. Handle residual quantities via rejection location.
7. Avoid intrusive changes in standard launch module.
SECTION 3 — ZPA Functional Solutions

The divisions are a structuring element of the activity, as products are not stored in the

Version 1.0
For example, CPD (consumer) handles large volumes, often full pallets, while LPD (luxury)
manages smaller volumes, with a high proportion of mezzanine picking.
Within each division, some products are distinguished:
• Either by their level of danger (aerosols, risk levels)
• Or by their specific use (PLV – point-of-sale advertising)
Some items have a lot number with an expiration date (DLUO) automatically calculated
from decoding the lot.
Others require an additional scan during preparation to ensure tracking of the AD Code –
equivalent to a serial number – particularly for LPD and PPD divisions, for traceability and
anti-fraud purposes.
These specificities lead to the coexistence of multiple storage and management rules.
These will be detailed in the corresponding section. Their implementation required several
specific developments, including:
• Entry of logistic data upon receipt
• Batch decoding
• AD Code tracking
Finally, the activity includes a copacking component, i.e., the creation of commercial
bundles grouping multiple products.
This flow relies on:
• Preparation of components via DO Copacking
• Then, after assembly, receipt of the BOM ASN
This activity is generally performed under a specific quality code "RLSC".
There are also two other types of ASN:
• INB (international)
• PPP (local product)
To conclude, the activity also includes management of customer returns, divided into two
categories:
• Cancellation (with reference)

AGL – L’Oréal Maroc – WMS Speed – Support Maintenance
Version 1.0
• Return (without reference)
Cancellation can be total or partial. A specific process allows flagging the order to be
canceled (status "shipped" mandatory). This flag automatically generates an expected
receipt and corresponding reception.
Returns, on the other hand, are performed manually, via creation of a reception without
expected receipt.
• III. Layout
Locations
Location nomenclature: LO001A001
All L'Oréal locations begin with the prefix "LO".
The next three digits identify the aisle.
The following letter indicates the level, with letter A corresponding to ground level.
In the pallet rack picking area, an intermediate beam was created between levels A and B
to store cartons in dynamic picking.
This beam is identified by the letter C. Ground level A is generally dedicated picking.
The last three digits of the location code determine the lateral position on the beam.
The warehouse is divided into two main zones:
• A pallet racking zone, corresponding to aisles 01 to 14
• A mezzanine zone, dedicated to shelf storage (cartons only), covering locations 300
to 500 in dynamic picking.

• IV. Storage Rules
There are three main storage rules, each with a specific role in flow management:
1. Rule 00001 – Reserve location search
o Applied by default on items and during reception
o Directs products to standard reserve locations
2. Rule 00002 – Replenishment to picking (ZPA)
o Used to direct picking replenishments to appropriate mezzanine locations,
particularly via ZPA transfer
o Ensures proper distribution of reserve stock to dynamic picking zones
3. Rule 00003 – Global picking storage
o Used for direct storage in picking zone, particularly from reception
o Unlike rule 00002, it also includes storage in dedicated picking locations
(often on pallet racks)

AGL – L’Oréal Maroc – WMS Speed – Support Maintenance
Version 1.0
o Includes a specific to control the maximum picking stock threshold
configured on each item, to avoid exceeding defined capacity
Detail rule 0001: Reserve storage
The first four storage rules direct products to caged rack zones, dedicated to storage of
dangerous products such as aerosols.
These rules are specific to each division, to ensure separation compliant with safety
requirements.
The next four rules guide standard products of each division to their respective storage
zones, according to typology and associated management mode.
Finally, the last two rules direct obsolete products or those with quality issues to dedicated
closed zones, intended for this type of treatment.
Detail rule 0003: Picking storage
The first five rules concern items classified as "fixed picking".
They search for a location in fixed picking zones of type LO_PICKING_XXXX (where XXXX
corresponds to the quality code).
The next eleven rules intervene to complete an existing location, based on:
• Available volume
• Various item criteria (aerosol level, PLV type, division, etc.)
Finally, the last eleven rules correspond to free searches.
They allow finding a new location in the same zones as before, with the same breakdowns
(aerosols, PLV, division), but they additionally integrate the picking threshold defined in the
item master data (2 or 5).
This threshold represents the maximum number of locations authorized in dynamic picking
for the same item.
For more details on configuration of these rules, refer to document SPD 020.
Detail rule 0002: ZPA storage used in dynamic picking transfer
This rule contains sequences similar to rule 00002.
• First, a first sequence completes an existing location based on available volume
• The next sequence searches for a new location in the appropriate zone

AGL – L’Oréal Maroc – WMS Speed – Support Maintenance
Version 1.0
• The main difference with previous free searches is the absence of picking threshold
control: this rule being used in the context of replenishment, it must accept all
location proposals
• Finally, a last control sequence detects failure cases (no applicable sequence). In
this case, the ZPA transfer is not blocked: the support is redirected to a reject
location, where it must be processed manually by the responsible party.
• V. Replenishment Rules
In the AGL – L'Oréal Morocco warehouse, several divisions coexist, each with different
volumes and order typologies.
To respond to all preparation modes, picking layout is managed according to two distinct
approaches:
1. Dedicated picking (classic)
→ Locations are fixed and reserved for specific items
2. Dynamic picking
→ Managed via transfer to Advanced Preparation Zone (ZPA), allowing flexible
allocation of locations based on operational needs
Classic dedicated picking replenishment
A picking location—generally located at the first level of the pallet rack—is reserved for a
specific item.
In this case, the item is classified as "fixed picking" and has a picking layout defined in its
parameters.
Note that each fixed picking layout should always contain two lines:
• One with the standard quality code corresponding to the division
• A second with the RLSC quality code, associated with copacking activity
This configuration ensures that products attached to the RLSC quality code can also be
replenished in the context of copacking order preparation.
This operation is standard in SPEED: replenishment is automatically triggered at order
launch when the available quantity in the dedicated location is insufficient to cover the
need.

AGL – L’Oréal Maroc – WMS Speed – Support Maintenance
Version 1.0
Dedicated replenishment configuration:
• Replenishment is limited to the need of the current wave
• The replenishment handling unit corresponds to the complete support: the system
will therefore seek an entire support in reserve, whether or not it corresponds to the
pallet handling unit
Dynamic picking replenishment
Dynamic picking replenishment—i.e., on locations without fixed picking layout (when an
empty location can be replaced by any other reference)—is not managed by standard in
SPEED.
To respond to operational needs, we implemented the ZPA transfer, associated with some
specifics.
Recall that ZPA transfer is an anticipated process that relies on the order portfolio to bring
down the need to a specific picking zone, which will then be targeted during order launch.
Objectives for L'Oréal:
1. Bring down only unit needs, not full pallet needs, already covered by complete
support picking 006 in launch parameters
2. Avoid complete support replenishment (standard SPEED) and allow choosing a
partial quantity to bring down, to optimize space in dynamic picking, often heavily
utilized
ZPA transfer configuration:
The ZPA transfer is configured according to this logic:
• Maximum handling unit to consider: CASE (to not take complete support need)
• Origin storage zone: all reserve stock
• Destination zone: LO_ZPA LOREA (dynamic locations, whether in mezzanine or
pallet rack (level C))
• And finally targets only items whose classification is items/Type_Picking/Dynamic
ZPA transfer calculation is based on orders having a preparation date.
By default, no preparation date is sent down, which allows the scheduler to precisely target
orders on which they wish to trigger ZPA transfer—in other words, only those for which a
preparation date has been entered.

AGL – L’Oréal Maroc – WMS Speed – Support Maintenance
Version 1.0
Support status management:
By default, ZPA transfer generates equipment operator transfers with status 03.
A specific was added to allow generation of replenishments with support at status 04.
Process harmonization:

This operation allows performing partial replenishment, adjusted to minimum need.
For example, if the need is 200 units, the system will bring down the entire support to cover

• Orange flag: ZPA transfer

• VI. Description of Different Reception Processes
There are several types of ASNs (expected receipts), as mentioned previously.
The reception process is identical for INB, PPP and BOM ASNs.
From creation of the expected receipt by the interface, the system automatically generates
the associated reception.
This reception initially contains no lines, as effective stock creation is performed via the
"Multi BL Reception" radio module, renamed for the occasion "ASN Reception".
Generally:
• Reception of non-expected items is not authorized
• Reception of quantities greater than those expected is not authorized either

Regarding returns, the process differs:
there is no expected receipt transmitted by the client.
Choice of items and quantities to receive is therefore left to the discretion of the operator in
charge of return processing.
Radio module multi BL reception (without expected receipt)
For return management, operators will be able to create a reception without expected
receipt via the menu -> reception without expected receipt and the RETURN tab.
They can then receive any item and quantity. The applied quality code is RL98.
They generally use generic labels for creation of support identifiers.
Classic radio module multi BL reception
The reception module is configured to successively request:
1. The BL number
2. Then the support number
Several decoding mechanisms were implemented at this stage to allow interpretation of
EAN128 labels containing:
• The SSCC of the support
• The item code
• And the lot number
The SSCC number is generally retained to identify complete supports in the system.
Reception-specific specifics:
Two SPDs modify radio behavior in reception:
• SPD09: Authorizes entry of complementary logistic data, such as:
o Item dimensions
o Weight
o Expiration date tracking
o Pallet and case handling units
• SPD011: Allows automatic decoding of manufacturing date from lot number
Regarding SPD09, distinguish two distinct data groups:

Version 1.0
• Item dimensions: If at least one item dimension or weight is not entered, the
dimension entry window will be displayed after creation of a first support
• Traceability data: Traceability will be requested only once, at first reception of the
item as well as mandatory pallet and case handling units
Regarding SPD011, it triggers if the item is checked lot1 tracked. The system requests the
lot number (if not recovered from the initially scanned EAN128).
Automatic calculation of manufacturing dates and expiration date (from product shelf life
present in item master data and decoded manufacturing date).
For decoding rules of manufacturing date from lot, refer to SPD 011.
Reception closure
Reception is closed in admin.
Logistic closure is mandatory before proceeding to final closure.
SPD015 intervenes at this stage:
it automatically deletes expected receipt lines for which there remain non-received
quantities.
Indeed, the remainder is not managed in SPEED, but directly in the host system (ERP SAP).
If a remainder must be processed, a new expected receipt will be generated and sent down
by SAP.
Important note:
A SAP constraint prevents reception of an expected receipt line at 0.
By default, the EDI interface enters 1 unit when the quantity to receive is zero.
A stock discrepancy is then corrected manually on both sides by operators.
Post-reception
Created supports are stored progressively by equipment operators, as operations proceed,
via the equipment operator storage transaction.
They have the possibility to manually switch to rule 0003 to perform direct storage in
picking zone, if necessary.
No allocation is possible from reception docks:
as long as merchandise is not physically stored and validated in stock, it remains nonallocatable.

• VII. Description of Different Preparation Processes: Launch to Shipping
General Information
Order launch is performed on the fly, orders rarely being sent down in advance.
Similarly, ZPA transfer is triggered just before each wave launch, to supply picking zones as
close as possible to real need.
Several wave launches are performed throughout the day.
Replenishments are performed hot and prioritized dynamically based on immediate needs
of preparers.
The flowchart below presents the steps of the preparation process from order launch to
shipping.
Preparation Steps:
1. Selection of order batch to launch and modification of preparation date
2. Launch of availability calculation
3. Control of shortages and correction if possible (using stock view/allocated orders ->
allocated and shortage orders) -> a specific view is used in the Stock screen, order
in entry
4. Launch of ZPA transfer
5. Launch of orders
6. Printing of carton picking and reserve reports
Preparation:
Use of radio module: multi-order preparation
1. Choice of mission type
2. Scan of mission number displayed on picking report (one or several)
3. Beginning of picking process (scan location, scan item, then enter quantity)
4. If item 'AD code' tracked, scan as many AD numbers as units to pick for LPD or as
cases for PPD
5. Scan of drop support (prepared support)
6. Deposit of supports in the finalization location at end of preparation

Finalization:
Each support is scanned via the finalization module, weight is entered and the support is
finalized.
Once all supports are finalized, the order passes to packed status and SHP is sent.
The client then sends back an order update with the invoice number, payment method and
shipping conditions.
Once this information is updated, the shipping report is printed by operators then attached
to the load.
The client also sends an invoice by email which is printed and attached to shipping
documents.
Note: The load creation process and support loading is not yet used by operators but was
part of new needs identified in the functional analysis.

4. Stock service PST allocation on dynamic picking locations in mezzanine
LO_ZPA_MEZZ

including copacking on zone LO_PICKING_XXXX (XXXX = quality code, RC01 RL01
RA01 RP01 RLSC)
6. Stock service for copacking in RLSC on zone LO_ZPA_LOREA
7. Missing service to recover what passed availability control but was not allocated on

• VIII. Description of Interfaces and EDI Operation
General file exchange operation
Exchanged files transit via L'Oréal's SFTP server:
• The OUTBOUND directory contains files deposited by L'Oréal for AGL

AGL – L’Oréal Maroc – WMS Speed – Support Maintenance
Version 1.0
• The INBOUND directory contains files generated by AGL and retrieved by L'Oréal
Downstream flow (L'Oréal → SPEED)
1. Flat files (in text format, separated by tabs) are retrieved by the WebMethods service
2. WebMethods converts the flat file to a JSON format API call
3. This call is transmitted to BK System's LINKUP service, which:
o Interprets the JSON
o Then updates SPEED with received data
Return flow (SPEED → L'Oréal)
1. Similarly, WebMethods performs recurring calls to LINKUP APIs
2. As soon as data is available, LINKUP returns JSON content
3. WebMethods converts this JSON to a flat file (.txt), then deposits it on L'Oréal's SFTP
in the corresponding directory
LINKUP marking management
LINKUP marking relies on the KEYU of the main table.
It allows identifying already transmitted data, to send them only once.
If needed, it is possible, via SpeedService, to delete the marking to make elements
available again during the next API call.
INBOUND Flows
ASN
There are 3 types of ASN in the EDI flow:
• PPP → Local ASN from Morocco
• INB → International ASN
• BOM → ASN allowing creation of copack bundles
The difference between PPP and INB lies in the presence of an inbound number in the case
of INB in addition to the Purchase order number. For PPP, both fields will have the same
value.
Return and cancellation ASNs are outside EDI. They are created from Speed, see ASN
return section.

Version 1.0
BOM ASN specificities:
The BOM ASN sent by the client contains a header line representing the quantity of bundle
to create. It serves to create the BOM ASN.
In the client file, BOM ASN lines represent components constituting the bundle. They serve
to create DO COPACK.
ASN Return
There are two types of ASN return:
• Cancellation (with reference), partial or total
• Customer return without reference
Creation of return and cancellation expected receipts is not sent down by the client.
The process differs depending on return type.
Cancellation:
We implemented a specific internal EDI flow via linkup that allows creating a reception
expected receipt matching the order being canceled (the reception is also created by
interface).
To trigger it, operators simply check the cancellation_order_creation_expected_auto box
and enter a cancellation_reason_code.
The return expected receipt is created with the invoice number as order reference. The flow
runs approximately every 5 minutes.
Operators can then receive items as for a classic reception either totally (order entirely
canceled) or partially. It is important to properly ship the reception to send back the good
receipt message to L'Oréal.
Return:
Returns without reference are created directly from the radio. Using the multi BL reception
module, then reception without expected receipt and finally the Return tab.
Similarly, ASN closure will trigger generation of the GR message.
An additional operation is nevertheless required in this case: enter the following
complementary information (beginning with 'return' + receptionType) in the reception
header.
If this information is missing (particularly receptionType), no message will be sent back.

AGL – L’Oréal Maroc – WMS Speed – Support Maintenance
Version 1.0
Distribution Order
The distribution order flow is classic, orders are typed 'customer_order' in the
complementary information OPE_ALPHA11 (unlike do Copack which are typed
'copack_order').
OUTBOUND Flows
In most transactional outbound flows, a unique WMSTransactionNumber is sent back.
The host system (SAP) does not allow integration of multiple messages with the same
wmsTransactionNumber.
It is sometimes necessary to resend a message that was in error in SAP. In this case, a new
WMSTransactionNumber must be used.
We therefore sometimes use in the JSON a forceReprocessingFlag. If this is at 1, then
WEBMETHODS will modify the transaction number by adding a suffix XXXXXX_1 XXXXXX_2
XXXXXX_3 and so on, depending on the number of times the message is reprocessed.
This allows bypassing the SAP constraint that accepts only one unique
WMSTransactionNumber per flow.
Good Receipt
The GR flow is triggered by complete closure of the expected receipt (logistic closure is not
sufficient).
Good Receipt Return
The GR return flow is triggered by closure of the return ASN (cancellation or return).
Pay attention to properly enter complementary information in the case of RETURN (see
ASN return section above).
In the case of cancellation, information is directly retrieved from the order during creation
of the expected receipt and reception.
Shipment Confirmation
The preparation declaration is triggered when the order passes to status 060, packed.
Note: Order shipping does not trigger any flow.
However, it is not possible to ship an order as long as we have not received the doupdate
(i.e., as long as the invoice number is not entered on the order's IC) -> SPD 026

Creation of a Manufacturing Order (MO)
Access

Structure of a Manufacturing Order
An MO consists of two main parts: Header and Lines.
Header
The header contains essential information for the MO:
Mandatory fields:
1. MO Reference – unique identifier of the manufacturing order.
2. Product Reference – the finished product to be manufactured.
3. Quantity – number of units of the finished product to produce.
Optional fields:
• Production area
• Production dates
• Traceability elements (lot, serial number, etc.)
• Template tick (to save the MO as a template for future use)
Quantities Summary:
• Shows the breakdown of total units into different Stock Units (SU) like
pallets, packages, and units.
Lines (Components)
Each line represents a component needed for the finished product.
Key points:
• Specify the quantity of the component required per finished product unit.
• Choose consumption type:
Sensitivity: Internal

o Automatic – system deducts components when production is
confirmed.
o Declarative – user manually declares the consumption.
Serial Number Management:
• If components and finished product manage serial numbers, the MO can
inherit serial numbers of components (only for single-unit components).
Tabs available for lines:
• Particularities – traceability, tolerances, etc.
• Replenishment – picking replenishment info
• Info – general information about the line
Line operations:
• Modify quantity or quality directly via contextual menu
• Disable obsolete lines (double-click → Info tab → Tick disabled)
Template Option
• An MO can be saved as a template for future use.
• Activate template mode via the Template tick.
• Obsolete lines can be disabled while keeping the MO as a template.
Activation of the MO
The MO must be activated before production can start:
Methods:
1. Contextual menu (right-click → Activate)
2. Change status in Info tab of the MO form
Info tab also tracks:
• Date & time of creation, modification, activation, and closing
• User who performed each action

Miscellaneous transactions section).

Workshop Approach
Access
• Menu: Manufacturing → Workshop Approach
• Opens a window where the user selects the workshops (production areas)
concerned by the operation.
Purpose
• Before production can start via radio frequency (RF) transactions, the
required component quantities must be approached (moved) to the
workshop.
• The system will move stock supports (containers, pallets, etc.) from storage
to the workshop for manufacturing.
How it Works
1. MO & Production Area Link
o Each Manufacturing Order (MO) is associated with a production area
(workshop).
2. Stock Movement
o From the MO lines, the system updates the status of stock supports to
Status 03, indicating they are ready for the workshop.
3. Operator Validation
o Operators validate these movements via RF transactions to confirm
that components are physically in the workshop.
4. Location Search Rules
o If the rule moves goods directly to the production location, they are
ready for immediate use.
o If the rule moves goods to a storage area in the workshop, the RF
Approach Workshop transaction must be used to move them to the
production location.
Key Notes
Sensitivity: Internal

• This step ensures that all components are physically available at the correct
workshop before production begins.
• It prevents shortages during manufacturing and ensures traceability of
components moved to the workshop.
Sensitivity: Internal

Management).

These parameters determine how components are approached (moved) to the

Key Configuration Options
1. Manufacturing Location

o Only one location per workshop area can be defined as the
manufacturing location.
2. Replenishment Methods
o Transfer by Support
▪ Moves a complete support (full pallet) for production.
▪ Configuration options:
▪ Origin stock area: area where components are picked
from.
▪ Search rule: defines where components are moved
within the workshop.
▪ Selected item family: specifies which items are
affected.
Sensitivity: Internal

▪ Horizon (Nb days): number of days in the MO portfolio
considered for quantity calculation.
o Pick-List
▪ Generates a transfer order for components matching the MO
requirements (rounded to the configured Stock Unit).
▪ Configuration options:
▪ Recipient: internal order destination (the workshop
location).
▪ Preparation channel: defines the channel used for the
generated order.
▪ Preparation type: must be Replenishment.
▪ Approach time (Nb days): initializes the preparation and

Purpose
• Ensures that all required components are available in the workshop before
production starts.
• Configures whether full pallets or quantities per pick-list are used for
replenishment.
• Integrates with MO portfolio horizon to calculate the required quantities in
advance.

Availability Calculation Overview
Purpose:
• Optional step before launching orders in preparation.
• Determines whether selected orders can be fully served based on current
stock availability.
• Helps identify if restocking a preparation area is necessary before picking.
Access:
• Configured in SpeedWMS for selected orders prior to launch.
Types of Availability Rates
1. Absolute Rate
o Calculated for the entire warehouse.
o Provides an overall availability of items.
o Considers the total need of the orders.
2. Proximity Rate
o Calculated for an advanced preparation zone.
o Determines if goods transfers to this zone are required.
o Total need is taken into account.
3. Retail Rate
o Calculated for areas where retail withdrawals occur.
o Only considers the requirement outside full pallets.
o Useful for small-quantity or picking operations.
Key Notes
• Not all three rates need to be configured; only the required rate can be set.
• Provides a pre-launch check to optimize stock allocation and reduce
preparation delays.
• The calculated rates can influence launch decisions, especially if stock is
insufficient.

Launch in Preparation – Overview
The launch in preparation is the process that takes orders from entry and assigns
stock to order lines, generating preparation missions and eventually preparation
notes (PNs).
Key Principles
1. Execution Scope
o Can be executed for one or more orders simultaneously.
o Each order line is processed individually based on stock availability
and service rules.
2. Missions
o A mission groups samples (stock assignments) created during launch.
o One mission can include multiple orders.
o One order can be split across multiple missions.
o Missions form the basis for preparation notes (PN).
Process Flow per Order Line
For each order line, SpeedWMS will:
1. Find procedures for sample creation
o These are the pre-configured rules for generating stock allocations.
2. Check application conditions
o Activity, recipient, item, and other filters defined in the procedure.
o Only applicable order lines are processed.
3. Apply stock search conditions
o Check zones, SU (stock units), and other stock parameters.
o Only unblocked stock is considered.
4. Create samples
o Each sample is an assignment of stock to an order line, including:
▪ Item
Sensitivity: Internal

▪ SU (stock unit)
▪ Quality
▪ Location
▪ Quantity
o Sample types:
1. Sample from stock – Direct allocation from stock.
2. Picking sample – Allocation from the picking location.
3. Missing sample – When stock is insufficient.
5. Ensure fulfillment
o Multiple samples may be created until the sum of all samples = order
line quantity.
Mission Generation Rules
• The portfolio of created samples is analyzed to generate missions.
• Rules are applied sequentially and are defined by application criteria such
as:
o Activity
o Zone
o Type of sample
o Reason
o Recipient
• Generation parameters determine:
o How withdrawals are sorted.
o Break rules that trigger the creation of a mission.
Each sample must belong to a mission before the process is considered complete.
Summary
Sensitivity: Internal

Step Description
1 Select orders for launch
2 Apply procedures to create samples per order line
3 Check stock availability and generate missing samples if needed
4 Group samples into missions based on configured rules
5 Missions are then used to generate Preparation Notes (PNs)
Sensitivity: Internal

Launch Settings Overview
Access:
System / Launch
The launch settings in SpeedWMS allow you to configure and control each step of
the order processing launch, from start to finish.
Steps of the Launch Process
Step Code Purpose
Launch start LAN_STAT_LAN Initializes the launch
Start of order LAN_START_CDE Prepares each order for processing
Start line processing LAN_START_LIN Prepares each order line
Line processing LAN_TRT_LIN Core processing of each line (main focus)
End of line processing LAN_END_LIN Finalizes processing of the line
End of order LAN_END_CDE Finalizes the order
End of launch LAN_END_LAN Wraps up the entire launch
Typically, the main configurations are needed for line processing and end of
launch.
Procedures for Order Line Processing
When processing each order line (LAN_TRT_LIN), the following procedures can be
executed sequentially:
1. Availability check – Checks stock and generates missing/backorder samples
if stock is insufficient.
2. Service on stock (pallets) – Proposes complete pallet samples from
available stock.
3. Picking service – Offers retail samples in the picking area based on stock
availability.
4. Service on stock (details) – Provides smaller quantities or detailed
withdrawals not handled by the previous step.
Sensitivity: Internal

5. Missing service – Any remaining quantities that couldn’t be served are
marked as missing.
Procedure Configuration
Each procedure can be configured along three main axes:
1. Application Settings Tab – Specifies which order lines the procedure applies
to.
2. Search Parameters Tab – Defines the stock constraints or search rules.
3. Generation Parameters Tab – Determines how the samples (direct debit
lines) should be generated.
The generated direct debit lines constitute the preparation mission lines.
End-of-Launch Processing (GenereMissionLan)
Once direct debit lines are generated:
• Lines are grouped into missions based on specified criteria.
• Configuration focuses on:
1. Which lines are included in missions (Application Settings).
2. How lines are grouped (Generation Parameters).
Example:
• Standard SpeedWMS setup generates one mission per picking area for an
activity order.
• Multiple mission generation procedures can be configured depending on the
rules.
Key Notes
• Launch settings allow complete automation of order line processing.
• You can define how stock is allocated, how missions are grouped, and how
missing items are handled.
• Proper configuration ensures preparation missions are generated efficiently
and logically.
Sensitivity: Internal

Launching a Distribution
Access:
Preparation / Distribution
Steps to Launch a Distribution
1. Select the distribution(s) you want to process.
2. Use the contextual menu and choose:
GO: Validate the distributions
What Happens When You Launch
• Orders are generated based on the distribution model.
• Orders are automatically validated (depending on configuration).
• Picking notes and labels are created for the orders.
• Optional: Print a label per recipient or per shipping support using the Print
markup labels option.
Notes
• Launching a distribution is the step that converts received goods into
prepared orders.
• Ensures that the distribution is ready for picking and shipping.
• Labels can be customized per recipient for easier handling.

Operations on ''in seizure'' orders
There are various operations accessible via the contextual menu on the portfolio of

Order Distribution
This function automatically distributes received goods to different customers
according to predefined models and can transform received products into
prepared products immediately.
Steps in the Distribution Process
Step 1: Creation of Models
• Define recipient codes (customers).
• Specify distribution percentages for each recipient.
• If percentages aren’t fixed, the model can be created with 0%, and
percentages can be entered later after importing data.
Step 2: Creation of the Distribution Header
• Import the distribution model.
• Enter the supplier code for the received goods.
Step 3: Entry of Lines to be Received
• Input the items and quantities to be received, as usual in receipt entry.
Step 4: Generation of the Distribution
• Validation triggers the automatic actions:
1. Stock creation – the received goods are added to stock.
2. Creation of different orders – based on the distribution model.
3. Validation of the different orders – automatically confirms them.
4. Edition of validation notes – prepares documents for reference.
Note: You can configure the system to not automatically validate orders, if needed.
Key Points:
• Distribution can be automatic and immediate, turning receipts into prepared
products.
• Percentages can be preset or updated post-import.
Sensitivity: Internal

• Validation of orders can be automatic or manual, depending on
configuration.

Adding Order Lines

templates, import, etc.).

Modifying Order Lines

Deleting Order Lines

Reordering Lines

Order Splitting
Purpose
• Allows the fragmentation of an order: splitting certain items or quantities
into a separate order.
• Useful when you need to process part of an order immediately or for
logistical reasons.
Access
• Contextual menu on the order to be split → select Split Order.
Process
1. The system displays:
o The original order
o The quantity for each item reference
2. User specifies the quantity for the second order in the field:
o "Spread quantity order 2"
3. Validate the input.
4. A confirmation screen appears.
Result
• A second order is created with the specified quantities.
• The new order inherits the header information of the original order
(customer, delivery details, etc.).
• Original order is updated with the remaining quantities.

Order Templates
Access
• Menu: Preparation → Orders Templates (in the SpeedWMS ribbon)
Purpose
• Simplifies order entry.
• Supports set concept: ensures items grouped as a set are handled together
during preparation.
Template Management
• Display all configured templates (customer or supplier orders).
• If no template exists, the system opens the create template screen
automatically.
• Options available for each template:
o Create new template
o Modify existing template
o Delete template
Template Details
For each template, you define:
1. Template name / code
2. Description of the template
3. List of items included in the template, with the quantity for each item
Set Concept
• By enabling the set option, the template is treated as inseparable:
o During preparation, if any element is in insufficient quantity, the
system only allows the preparation of complete sets.
o This ensures all items of a set are included together and prevents
partial sets from being processed.
Sensitivity: Internal

Orders Management
Access
• Menu: Preparation → Orders
Purpose
• Provides a portfolio of all orders in SpeedWMS.
• Orders are organized into tabs based on their status.
• Default filter: Creation date in a specific viewing period.
• Filters can be customized by:
o Creation date
o Preparation date
o Delivery date
o Printing date
o Wave release date
o Modification date

Introduction - Packaging
The Packaging Management module is used to manage exchanges and management of
packaging stocks(used for transport) between the different partners.
This is a licensed module.
The term "Packaging" is used in logistics to designate all the packaging exchanged
through the flows made between the different partners. The type of packaging (EUR
CHEP pallets, shelves, bins, etc.) makes it possible to identify the packaging.
The packaging supporting the goods delivered to a warehouse is placed on
consignment:
• At loading : the supplier deposits X number of pieces of equipment with the carrier.
The carrier is obliged to return all the equipment it has received. This can be done
immediately upon loading or afterwards. The consignment voucher will then make it
possible to record the flows of packaging in progress.
• On delivery: the principle remains the same, the carrier records the number of pieces
of packaging delivered to the recipient, as well as the number of pieces that the latter
has returned to him.
The management of the packaging consists in monitoring the exchanges of packaging
between the three partners mentioned.
For this, it is essential to master certain concepts before using the module.
Packaging accounts
The packaging accounts represent the different third parties that interact in the logistics
environment that we manage.
Two types of packaging accounts exist:
.External accounts: represent all external third parties with which exchanges take
place. These will essentially be carriers, suppliers and consignees.
Sensitivity: Internal

.Internal accounts: represent the stock of equipment for the logistics sites managed by
SpeedWMS (or another ERP).
In general there is one account per site. However, for service providers it is common for
pallet stocks to be separated by customer; in this case several accounts are created.
There may also be breakage and loss of equipment. Inventories and adjustment
operations must therefore be carried out. Packaging purchases can also be made from
“Packaging Merchants”. These operations will be recorded on a dedicated third-party
account, of the external type.
Management of the packaging accounts
The management of packaging accounts allows each participant to determine at any
time and for each type of packaging:
.- The number of packaging that each partner owes him
.- The number of packaging he owes to each partner
.- Committed stock of tackle on handling units
.- The free stock of packaging he has left on site
.- The valuation of the various stocks of packaging
Several solutions exist to settle accounts with partners:
➢Packaging are due to a partner:
.It is possible to trigger a delivery of packaging, if we have free stock
.Bills can be received for packagings, if there is no free stock. A market price exists for
each type of packaging and for each partner.
➢• A partner owes us equipment:
.- The partner can have the equipment he needs delivered.
Sensitivity: Internal

.- The packaging can be invoiced to the partner. Transfer prices are negotiated between
the partners for each type of packaging.
SpeedWMS’ default currency is the Euro, but it can be changed. (Access: System /
Global settings / Miscellaneous section / Language)
Packaging movements
Each of the packaging account management solutions will be subject to an account-toaccount movement of packaging: an entry on the first account generates an exit on the
second, and vice versa.
Specialized third-party accounts generate various movements which therefore do not
appear in the packaging movements.
The movement type determines the file from which the movement was generated:
▪A receiving
▪Order preparation
▪An expedition
For example, an packaging movement resulting from a reception will be identified by the
reception number.
The status indicates whether the movement is validated or simply entered (040 or 010).
Indeed, the input operations will directly initialize the movements. We can make
mistakes and therefore adjust until validation.
This allows you to update the packaging counters.

SOP: Creating a Receipt Header (GRN) in Speed WMS
Sensitivity: Internal
1. Purpose
To define the standard procedure for creating a receipt header (GRN) in Speed WMS
in order to formally declare incoming goods before stock creation and processing.
2. Accessing the Receipt Creation Screen
The receipt creation function can be accessed by:
• Selecting Create Receipt from the contextual menu, or
• Clicking the Add (+) button in the Receipts module
Once opened, the receipt screen is divided into two sections:
• Upper section: Receipt Header
• Lower section: Receipt Lines (goods details)
3. Receipt Header – System-Initialized Fields
The following fields are automatically populated when the receipt form opens and
are not editable unless stated otherwise:
• Activity Code
o Represents the current Speed WMS environment
o Read-only field
• Speed Receipt Number (REE_NORE)
o System-generated internal counter
o Unique and non-modifiable
• Receipt Date and Time
o Defaults to the creation date and time
o Can be modified if required
• Default Reception Dock
o Pre-selected based on system configuration
Sensitivity: Internal

o Displays all dock-type locations available in the environment
4. Mandatory User-Defined Fields
The user must complete the following fields before saving the receipt:
• Customer Account (REE_CCLI)
o Required if the activity manages multiple customers
• Supplier / Third-Party Code
o Selected from the list of third parties configured in the environment
o A new third-party record can be created directly from the selection
screen
• Receipt Reference
o Alphanumeric field
o Optional but strongly recommended
o Facilitates searching and identification instead of using the Speed
receipt number
5. Receipt Lines (Goods Declaration)
• Goods are entered in the lower table of the receipt screen
• Each line represents an item declared on the receipt
• Lines are stored in REL_DAT once the receipt is saved
6. Outcome
After saving:
• A receipt header record is created in REE_DAT
• Associated receipt lines are created in REL_DAT
• The receipt becomes available for validation, storage, and downstream
processes (stock, movements, missions)
7. Related Tables
Sensitivity: Internal

• REE_DAT – Receipt Header
• REL_DAT – Receipt Lines
• STK_DAT – Stock (generated after validation)
• MVT_DAT – Movements

SOP: Creating Receipt Lines in Speed WMS
Sensitivity: Internal
1. Purpose
To describe the standard procedure for adding receipt lines to an existing receipt
header in Speed WMS.
Each receipt line represents one storage medium that will later be generated into
stock.
2. Prerequisite
• A receipt header must already exist and be open.
• Receipt lines are added before stock generation.
• No stock movement is created until stock generation is performed.
3. General Rules for Receipt Lines
Regardless of the input method used, the following rules always apply:
• Item code must exist
o It is not possible to receive an item that does not have an article
master (item sheet) in Speed WMS.
• Quantity is always stored in units per storage medium
o Even if entered in alternative logistic units, Speed converts and stores
quantities in units.
• Default quality
o Taken from the item sheet or the default activity configuration.
• Traceability fields
o Fields such as Lot, Lot2, DLC, DLUO, etc. are mandatory if configured
on the item sheet.
• Owner assignment
o Automatically populated if defined on:
1. The item sheet (priority), or
Sensitivity: Internal

2. The activity
o If no owner is predefined, the user must select one from the list of
authorized owners.
4. Minimum Required Information
Each receipt line requires at least:
• Item Code
• Quantity to be received
• Quality code
5. Methods for Adding Receipt Lines
Speed WMS provides multiple ways to add receipt lines. All methods create the
same result.
5.1 Direct Addition (Manual Entry)
• Enter the item code directly in the New Receipt Line field.
• Enter the quantity and quality.
• Validate to create the line.
Use case:
Fast entry when the item code is known.
5.2 Addition by Item Search
• Right-click in the Item Code field.
• Select Search for an Article.
• The system displays items linked to the receipt supplier.
• Enable All Suppliers to view all items in the activity.
• Select the item → item code is auto-filled.
• Enter quantity and quality, then validate.
Sensitivity: Internal

Use case:
When item code is unknown or needs confirmation.
5.3 Addition Using Item Templates (Grid Pattern)
• Right-click in the Item Code field.
• Select Item Templates.
• Choose a predefined template linked to the activity.
• Enter quantities:
o All column: same quantity for all references
o Individual columns: different quantities per reference
• Validate to generate multiple receipt lines at once.
Use case:
Bulk or standardized receipts.
5.4 Addition via Detailed Entry Form
• Double-click in the Item Code field.
• The detailed entry screen opens.
• Allows access to:
o All logistic units
o Traceability fields
o Advanced item attributes
• Mandatory traceability fields become editable if required by the item.
• Validate to create the receipt line.
Use case:
Complex items requiring traceability or advanced data entry.
5.5 Addition by Excel Import
• Click the Excel Import icon.
• Paste or import an Excel file containing exactly three columns in this order:
Sensitivity: Internal

1. Item Code
2. Quantity
3. Quality Code
Import options:
• Unknown Item Code column displays items not existing in Speed.
• Import First Line determines whether the first row is imported.
• Preview / Printing shows how data will be imported.
• Validate creates the receipt lines.
Use case:
Mass receipt creation from external systems.
6. Reception Dock Handling
• The reception dock is initially inherited from the receipt header.
• If the dock is changed on the header after lines already exist, Speed prompts
the user to:
1. Keep existing lines unchanged, or
2. Update the dock on all existing receipt lines
7. Receipt Line Status Before Stock Generation
• Receipt lines are saved but not yet in stock.
• Field Tick Stock Input remains set to 0.
• No stock movement (MVT_DAT) is created.
• Supplier expected quantities are not consumed yet.
• Receipt lines can still be:
o Modified
o Deleted
without impacting Speed history.
8. Stock Generation (Next Step)
Sensitivity: Internal

• Receipt lines only become stock after Stock Generation is executed.
• Stock generation:
o Creates records in STK_DAT
o Creates movement records in MVT_DAT
o Consumes expected quantities if linked to a supplier order

• STK_DAT – Stock
• MVT_DAT – Movements

o Expected Receipt Lines: REL_DAT (used when generating receipts)
o Receipt Header (after generation): REE_DAT

Before importing expected items, ensure that:
• You are logged into the correct activity (ACT_CODE)
• The supplier and customer account exist in Speed
• All item codes in the Excel file exist in the article master
• The Excel file follows the required format

2. Open the Expected menu
Sensitivity: Internal

3. Select an existing expected receipt or create a new one
4. Click the Import button
This action opens the Expected Items Import screen.

The import is performed using an existing Excel file.
5.1 Mandatory Column Structure
The Excel file must contain the expected items data in a predefined structure (as
configured in the activity).
Typically required fields include:
• Item Code
• Expected Quantity
• Quality Code
• (Optional depending on configuration)
o Lot
o DLUO / DLC
o Owner
Important
• Item codes must exist in Speed
• Traceability fields are mandatory if managed on the item sheet
• Quantities are interpreted in units per storage medium
6. Import Process
1. Click Import
2. Browse and select the Excel file
3. Load the file into the import screen
4. Review the imported data:
o Valid item codes
Sensitivity: Internal

o Quantities
o Quality codes
5. Validate the import
Once validated:
• Expected item lines are created
• The expected receipt is updated with imported lines
7. System Behavior After Import
After a successful import:
• Expected items are visible under Receiving → Expected
• No stock is created at this stage
• No movement is recorded
• The data is used later when:
o Creating a receipt
o Matching received quantities against expected quantities
8. Error Handling & Validation
8.1 Common Import Errors
Error Cause Resolution
Item not found Item code does not exist Create item or correct code
Missing traceability Lot / DLUO required Update Excel file
Quantity invalid Zero or non-numeric value Correct quantity
8.2 SQL Validation (Optional – Support Use)
SELECT *
FROM REL_DAT
WHERE ACT_CODE = 'RSAJHBJP'
Sensitivity: Internal

AND REE_NORE = 'EXPECTED_NUMBER';
Use this query to verify that:
• Expected lines were created
• Quantities and item codes are correct
9. Best Practices
• Always validate Excel data before importing
• Use expected items to:
o Reduce receiving errors
o Speed up receipt creation
o Improve traceability accuracy
• Do not import duplicate expected lines for the same receipt
• Keep the original Excel file for audit and troubleshooting

Concept Meaning

No Stock Impact Import does not generate stock

SOP: Management of Expected Receptions in Speed WMS
Sensitivity: Internal
1. Purpose
This SOP explains how to view, manage, and process expected receptions in Speed
WMS.
Expected receptions are used to anticipate incoming goods (purchase orders or
returns) before physical receipt and to control receiving accuracy.
2. Functional Scope
• Module: Receiving → Expected
• Business Process: Expected Receipts Management
• Applicable for:
o Purchase Orders
o Returns of Goods
3. Definition: Expected Reception
An expected reception line represents:
• A quantity of a specific item
• Expected to be received
• For a given order reference (usually supplier PO)
• With a planned receipt date
Each expected reception line is consumed when a corresponding stock entry
movement is created in Speed.
Important:
Expected receptions do not create stock on their own.
Stock is only created when a receipt is generated and validated.
4. Accessing Expected Receptions
1. Navigate to Receiving
Sensitivity: Internal

2. Select Expected
This opens the Expected Receptions Management screen, displaying all expected
reception data for the current activity.
5. Display Modes
Speed allows two different display modes for expected receptions.
5.1 Expected Reception Headers View
This view groups expected lines by expected reception header (order-level view).
Used when:
• Managing receipts by supplier or PO
• Initiating reception for multiple lines at once
5.2 Expected Items Portfolio View
This view displays individual expected item lines.
Used when:
• Managing quantities at item level
• Modifying or deleting specific expected lines
5.3 Configuring the Display Mode
The display mode is controlled via global settings:
Path:
System → Global → Module → Expected
The user must define whether the screen opens in:
• Header view
• Item portfolio (line-level) view
6. Status Management
Expected receptions are organized by status, which reflects their progression in the
receiving process.
Sensitivity: Internal

Typical lifecycle:
1. Expected created
2. Expected linked to a receipt
3. Quantity consumed when stock entry occurs
4. Expected closed once fully consumed
Consumption occurs only when an entry movement into stock is recorded.
7. Available Actions
From the Expected Receptions screen, users can:
7.1 Create Expected Reception Lines
• Manually create new expected lines
• Define item, quantity, quality, planned date
• Interface creation (external import) is also supported
7.2 Modify Expected Reception Lines
• Update quantities, dates, or references
• Changes can be applied:
o Individually
o Globally (bulk updates)
7.3 Import Expected Receptions from File
• Import a list of expected items (Excel or interface file)
• Used for bulk creation from supplier data or ERP
7.4 Delete Expected Reception Lines
• Allowed only if:
o The expected line is not already consumed
o No stock entry movement is linked
Sensitivity: Internal

• System constraints apply to prevent data inconsistency
7.5 Initiate the Reception Process
• Select one or more expected lines
• Use the contextual menu
• Associate selected expected lines with a Speed receipt
• This action launches the receipt creation process
8. Business Rules & Behavior
• One expected line = one planned receipt quantity
• Partial consumption is allowed
• Consumption = quantity received into stock
• Expected lines remain editable until consumption starts
• Once stock entry is validated, expected quantities are reduced
9. Data Model Reference (Support / RAG Context)
Object Table
Expected Reception Header REA_DAT
Expected Reception Lines REL_DAT
Receipt Header REE_DAT
Stock Entry Movement MVT_DAT
10. Common RAG Questions This SOP Answers
• What is an expected reception in Speed?
• How do expected receptions work?
• When is an expected quantity consumed?
• How do I initiate a receipt from expected items?
Sensitivity: Internal

• Can expected receptions be deleted or modified?
• Why does an expected line remain open after receipt creation?
11. Best Practices
• Always use expected receptions for planned deliveries
• Import expected items for large or repetitive receipts
• Do not delete expected lines that are partially consumed
• Validate expected data before linking to a receipt
• Use item-level view for detailed control
Sensitivity: Internal

SOP: Reception Handling Principles in Speed WMS
Sensitivity: Internal
1. Purpose
This SOP explains the two supported methods for handling receptions in Speed WMS,
including their use cases and operational principles.
2. Reception Handling Methods Overview
Receptions in Speed WMS can be managed using one of two methods:
1. Reception based on Expected Items
2. Reception based on Declarative Entry
Each method serves a different operational need and workflow.
3. Reception Based on Expected Items
3.1 Description
This method manages receptions using a portfolio of expected items. Expected items
represent advance arrival announcements or supplier purchase orders.
Expected items may be:
• Entered manually in Speed WMS
• Imported via an interface
• Synchronized from an external system (e.g., sales management or ERP system)
3.2 Operational Principle
• Each expected item defines:
o Item reference
o Expected quantity
o Order-giver reference
o Planned reception date
• During reception, received quantities are matched against expected
quantities.
Sensitivity: Internal

• When stock is received and an inbound stock movement is created, the
expected quantity is consumed.
3.3 Output and Controls
• At the end of the reception process, Speed WMS can generate a comparison
between expected quantities and received quantities.
• This method is recommended when:
o Purchase orders are known in advance
o Quantity reconciliation is required
o Supplier performance tracking is needed
4. Reception Based on Declarative Entry
4.1 Description
This method manages receptions without prior expected items. The reception is
created based on what is physically received at the warehouse.
4.2 Operational Principle
• Receptions are declared directly in the Reception module
• Item quantities are entered manually or via an interface
• No expected item comparison is required
4.3 Input Methods
Receptions can be performed using:
• Manual data entry
• Interface-fed data
• Radio Frequency (RF) module (see RF documentation)
4.4 Recommended Use Cases
This method is recommended when:
• Expected data is unavailable or unreliable
• Urgent or unplanned deliveries occur
• Simplified reception is required
Sensitivity: Internal

5. Method Selection Guidelines
Scenario Recommended Method
Known purchase orders Expected Items
Quantity reconciliation required Expected Items
Unplanned delivery Declarative Reception
RF-based reception Declarative or Expected
ERP-integrated workflow Expected Items
6. Related Modules
• Receiving / Expected
• Reception Module
• Stock Movement Module
• RF Module (refer to RF documentation)

SOP: Receipt Closure in Speed WMS
Sensitivity: Internal
1. Purpose
This SOP describes the receipt closure process in Speed WMS, including its
effects, constraints, and operational usage.
2. Definition of Receipt Closure
Receipt closure is the final step in the lifecycle of a Speed WMS receipt.
The closure operation freezes all receipt data and confirms the reception as
complete.
Once closed, the receipt becomes read-only.
3. Effects of Receipt Closure
After a receipt is closed:
• The receipt cannot be modified
• No new receipt lines can be added
• Existing receipt lines cannot be edited or deleted
• No new media or attachments can be added
However:
• The receipt remains accessible in consultation mode
• All attached documents can still be viewed and printed
• Receipt data can be used for reporting and audit purposes
4. System Integration Considerations
• Receipt closure is generally the trigger point for:
o Data feedback to external systems (n+1 systems)
o ERP or sales management system synchronization
• Only closed receipts should be considered final and reliable for downstream
processing
Sensitivity: Internal

5. How to Close a Receipt
Receipt closure is performed from the Receipt Management Screen using one of
the following methods:
• Contextual menu → Close Receipt
• Speed WMS command bar → Close Receipt button
Both methods perform the same operation and apply the same validation rules.
6. Preconditions for Closure
Before closing a receipt, ensure that:
• All receipt lines have been correctly recorded
• Quantities and item references are validated
• Required documents or media have been attached
• No further modifications are expected
7. Best Practices
• Close receipts only after full verification
• Avoid premature closure, as reopening is not possible
• Ensure closure is aligned with external system synchronization schedules
8. Related Modules
• Receipt Management
• Stock Movements
• Document Management
• ERP / n+1 System Interfaces
Sensitivity: Internal
