Support Break Management – RAG-Friendly Version
Purpose:
The support break feature allows Speed WMS to automatically split large incoming
quantities into multiple storage supports during receipt line creation, based on the
packaging plan defined in the item sheet.
1. Parameter Location
• Found in the Storage tab of each item sheet.
• Activated per stock unit (SU) type configured on the item.
• Determines how quantities are split across storage media when creating
receipt lines.
2. Behavior Without Support Break
• Example:
o Item pallet = 750 units
o Received quantity = 4 pallets → 3000 units
• If support break is not activated:
o A single receipt line will contain the entire 3000 units.
o To match the actual pallets, 4 separate receipt lines must be created
manually.
3. Behavior With Support Break Activated
• Support break activated on Pallet SU:
o System automatically splits the incoming quantity into multiple
storage supports according to the item’s packaging plan.
• Example:
o Received quantity = 10000 units
o Support break splits:
▪ 2 supports of 4500 units each
▪ 1 support for the remaining 1000 units
Sensitivity: Internal

• Benefits:
o Optimizes administrative entry of incoming goods
o Ensures receipt lines match the physical pallets received
4. Rules & Notes
• The number and size of supports generated depend on the item sheet
packaging plan.
• Only quantities that comply with the item’s packaging plan can be
automatically split.
• If the received pallets do not comply with the packaging plan, manual
adjustment is needed.
Sensitivity: Internal

Topic: Partial Validation of a Replenishment
Access Path: Within the Replenishment Window, right-click on a
mission/replenishment line and select the context menu option: "Partially validate
the mission".
Purpose: To confirm the completion of only a portion of the total quantity requested
in a replenishment task.
Process Steps:
1. Enter Completed Quantity: In the validation window, manually enter the
quantity that has actually been replenished and moved to the target picking
location.
2. Manage Remaining Quantity:
o The system will automatically calculate the remaining quantity
(original requested quantity minus the validated quantity).
o Optional Modification: You can manually override this automatic
calculation. Click the edit icon (pen) next to the "Remaining qty" field
to directly enter or adjust the remaining balance.
Result: The replenishment task is updated. The validated quantity is closed, and a
new replenishment line is typically created for the remaining quantity to be
completed later.
Sensitivity: Internal

Topic: Principle of Picking Replenishment
Core Concept: Replenishment is the process of moving stock to picking locations
to ensure availability for order fulfillment. Its setup and execution follow specific
rules.
1. Prerequisites & Setup
To enable the creation of replenishments, the following master data must be
configured:
• Picking Zones must be defined.
• Picking Locations must be established and associated with one or more
picking zones.
2. Replenishment Rules & Source Logic
• Source Restriction: A picking location can be replenished from another
picking location, provided the source location does not belong to the same
picking area (zone).
• Parameter Management: Replenishment rules (e.g., min/max levels) are
typically defined at the picking zone level.
o Exception & Priority: Specific parameters can be defined at the
individual item level. These item-specific settings take priority over
the zone-level parameters.
3. Execution & Validation Workflow
Launching a replenishment generates replenishment lines, which are initially
"orphan" task lines not yet assigned to a move.
• Generation: The process can be triggered manually or automatically (e.g., via
batch job).
• Validation Modes: These lines are converted into executable warehouse
transfers using one of three validation methods:
1. Administrative Validation: Confirmed directly from the list of
replenishment lines in the backend system.
2. Transfer Validation: Executed via the storage radio frequency (RF)
transaction on a mobile device, validating the physical transfer.
3. Replenishment Validation: Executed via the replenishment RF
transaction on a mobile device, validating the task at the
replenishment line level.
Sensitivity: Internal

4. Monitoring & Reports
• Replenishment List: A central list is available to view and manage all created
replenishment tasks.
• Anomaly List: A dedicated report can be generated on demand to identify
any issues or errors in the replenishment process (e.g., source shortages,
invalid parameters).
Sensitivity: Internal

Topic: Replenishment Generation
Access Path: Preparation / Replenish. → Click the 'Generate' button (located on the
right side of the interface).
Purpose: This function launches a process to calculate and create replenishment
tasks based on user-defined criteria.
1. Generation Window & Criteria
The Replenishment Generation Window is the interface where users define the
criteria for the system to calculate required replenishments.
• Primary Selection: You must first select the picking area (zone) concerned by
the generation.
• Granular Selection: Within the selected zone, you can further narrow the
scope by specifying:
o A single Item
o A single Location
o An Item Family
• Parameter Initialization: When a zone is selected, all other calculation
parameters (e.g., min/max levels) are automatically initialized with the
values defined for that zone.
2. Key Parameter: "Complete Pickings"
• Purpose: When enabled, this parameter directs the system to generate
replenishments with the sole goal of filling existing picking tasks, regardless
of the standard stock level requirements.
• Effect: It ensures that all items requested in open pickings are fully available
at the picking location.
3. Execution
• Process: After defining the criteria, click the dedicated
validation/confirmation button in the window.
• Outcome: This action triggers the system's calculation engine, which
processes the inputs and generates the specific replenishment tasks
desired by the user.
Sensitivity: Internal

Topic: Replenishment Management
Access Path: Preparation / Replenishment
Primary Function: To select and validate the movement of stock to picking
locations.
1. Replenishment Selection
You can initiate a replenishment task using several selection methods:
• Replenishment Window: The primary interface for selection.
• Picking Location: Select directly from a specific picking location that needs
stock.
• Specific Item: Select based on a particular item that requires
replenishment.
Filtering: After selecting a general Site, you can apply additional filters to narrow
the selection further based on:
• The collection site (where stock is taken from).
• The restocking drop-off site (where stock is delivered to).
2. Replenishment Validation
Replenishment tasks can be validated in two ways:
• Partial Validation: Confirm the completion of only a portion of the requested
replenishment quantity.
• Total Validation: Confirm the completion of the entire requested
replenishment quantity.
Note: For detailed procedures and rules governing validation, please refer to the
dedicated system documentation sections for validation.
Sensitivity: Internal

Access
• Menu: Settings / Location / Areas
• Select a picking replenishment zone (type 003) → Context menu →
Replenishment
The settings apply to all picking locations within the selected area.
Main Parameters for Picking Replenishment
1. Picking quality
o Defines the quality of items to be replenished at the picking location.
2. Areas of origin for replenishment
o Stock is taken from these areas.
o Multiple areas can be selected with priorities.
o Rule: Picking zones can only replenish from storage zones and vice
versa.
3. Picking expression unit
o Defines the unit used for picking (e.g., pallet, box).
o Converts the expression value into item stock units (SU).
4. Picking capacity
o Maximum quantity that can be picked (in picking expression units).
5. Replenishment trigger threshold
o Percentage threshold that triggers replenishment.
6. Activation if needed
o Enables replenishment if certain conditions are met.
7. Max quantity per replenishment line
o Defines the maximum quantity moved per replenishment line.
o Prevents exceeding transport limits; if blank, the entire need can be
moved at once.
8. Replenishment SU
o Specifies which stock unit (SU) to replenish.
Sensitivity: Internal

o Must be managed at the item master level.
o Can be replenished by package, pallet, or stock support.
9. Support
o Determines whether to replenish the entire stock support (full pallet,
bin, etc.), regardless of quantity.
Criteria for Replenishment Quantity
These determine how much to replenish:
1. Restrict to the need
o Replenish only the minimum quantity necessary.
2. Necessity replenishment
o Replenish at least one replenishment unit.
3. Saturation of the picking
o Always replenish the minimum needed to serve orders.
o Saturation only fills up to maximum picking quantity.
Note: The first three options are mutually exclusive.
4. Limit to max picking
o Ensures replenishment does not exceed the maximum picking limit.
5. Nature of replenishment
o Allows assigning a type or priority to replenishments for processing in
RF (e.g., standard, manual, scheduled).
6. Generation of transfer by forklift
o Creates transfer forecasts.
o Updates media status to 03 so operators can move stock.
Specific Sorting
• The “Specific sorting” tab controls the order in which stock lines are offered
for replenishment.
• Useful for prioritizing stock locations, oldest stock first, or specific zones.
Sensitivity: Internal

Restocking Calculation Method
Purpose:
• To determine the quantity of items to be replenished at a picking location,
taking into account current stock, orders in preparation, and thresholds.
Factors Considered:
1. Replenishment Unit: The unit used for replenishment (e.g., pallet, box).
2. Max Quantity at Picking: Maximum quantity that can be held at the picking
location.
3. Replenishment Threshold: Minimum quantity that triggers a replenishment if
stock falls below it.
4. Quantity in Orders in Preparation: Items already allocated to orders
currently in preparation.
Restocking Logic:
1. Check Orders in Preparation:
o If the item exists in orders in preparation and the current picking
quantity is less than the maximum at picking, a replenishment is
generated.
o Quantity to replenish = Max at picking – Quantity currently at picking
2. Check Replenishment Threshold:
o If the item is not in orders in preparation:
▪ If the current picking quantity < threshold, generate a
replenishment.
▪ If current picking quantity ≥ threshold, no replenishment is
generated.
Calculation Formula:
Need = AvailableQtyPicking – sum(PickingSamplingsNotValidated)
+ sum(REA_NotValidated) – ReplenishmentThreshold
Quantity to Replenish:
Sensitivity: Internal

QtyToReplenish = PicSamplQty + MaxPickingQty – PicAvailableQty
– ReplQty – QtyTransfToPick – QtyTransfFromPick
• Adjustments can be made depending on saturation, adding threshold
quantity or max picking quantity.
Example:
• Picking Unit: Pallet (1 pallet = 15 parcels)
• Picking Capacity: 2 pallets
• Threshold: 10% (3 parcels)
• Orders Launched: 45 parcels
• Current Quantity at Picking: 5 parcels
Calculation:
Quantity to Replenish = 45 + 30 – 5 = 70 parcels
• Optimal quantity to replenish: 70 parcels
• Minimum quantity needed to serve orders: 43 parcels
Sensitivity: Internal

Total Validation
Purpose:

Topic: Introduction to Sampling in Quality Control
Purpose: Sampling is a traceability feature designed to manage and document
quality controls for received goods.
Objective: To systematically extract a sample from incoming shipments. This
sample is used to perform various quality inspections, which determine whether
the received items are approved for use in order picking and fulfillment.
Core Process Principle
1. Trigger: The process is initiated automatically after stock generation during
the receiving process.
2. Rule Application: The system evaluates and applies the pre-configured
sampling rules stored in the global system configuration.
3. Rule Outcome: These rules define three key elements for the sample:
o The quantity to be taken.
o The quality status to assign.
o The destination location for the sample (if specified).
4. Physical Execution: The original received handling unit (e.g., pallet, carton) is
split or "burst." The defined sample quantity is separated and set aside.
5. Quality Gate: The segregated sample then undergoes quality control. The
result of this inspection dictates the fate of the entire received batch:
o If compliant, the batch proceeds to active stock.
o If non-compliant, the batch is quarantined or rejected.
Sensitivity: Internal

Topic: Automated Sampling During Receiving
Trigger: Sampling is automatically executed whenever stock is generated in
SpeedWMS, either through:
• The Administrative (backend) interface, or
• Radio Frequency (RF) transactions using reception modules (Standard
Reception, Multi-BL Reception).
Prerequisite: Sampling rules must be configured and active for the received items.
1. Process Overview & Example
When a receiving order matches an active sampling rule, the system automatically
creates a sample.
• Example Scenario:
o Items Received: G50OXF90 and G50OXFA3
o Applied Rule: For items in the "Standard paper" item family.
o Rule Action: Take 2 units, place them in location W01-B-01-0-1, and
assign the quality code CTRL.
2. Viewing Sampling Results
The results of automated sampling can be viewed at three levels in the system:
A. Storage Tab (of the Completed Receipt)
• Visual Impact: The original receipt lines appear "burst" or split. In the
example, four lines display instead of two.
• Sample Details: The sampled units are shown on a new, auto-incremented
support (handling unit).
• Status: They are located in the predefined sampling location with the CTRL
quality code.
• Special Case for Serial Numbers: If the item manages serial numbers, a
dedicated screen prompts the user to select the specific serial numbers for
the new sample support during the burst process.
B. Stock Movements
Three distinct stock movements are logged for each sampled item:
1. Receiving Input: The initial input of the full received quantity.
Sensitivity: Internal

2. Sampling Output: An output representing the quantity removed from the
original support for sampling (causing the support split).
3. Sampling Input: An input representing the creation of the new support
containing the sample quantity.
C. Events
The system logs events related to all receiving activities and the associated stock
inputs and outputs generated by the sampling process.
3. Important Configuration Note for RF Receiving
When receiving goods via SpeedRadio (RF):
• Operators must verify that "Stock generation" is enabled in the settings of
the specific reception module being used.
• All sampling-related settings must also be checked and correctly configured
for the automated process to function as intended.
Sensitivity: Internal

Topic: Configuration of Sampling Rules
Access Path: System / Receiving - Sampling
Purpose: Sampling rules define the logic for selecting items to undergo quality
control upon receipt. Rules are evaluated in priority order.
1. Rule Management & Creation
• Priority: Rules are listed and searched in order of their assigned priority.
• Creating a Rule: Click the "+" (Add) button to create a new rule.
• Rule Identification:
o A unique numeric ID is auto-assigned via incrementation.
o A default title is also auto-generated but can be modified by the user.
• Creation Methods: A rule can be configured using one of two methods
related to the sampling logic:
o Standard: Uses the predefined sampling parameters and logic built
into SpeedWMS (default).
o Free: Allows the user to directly input a custom code/query into a
dedicated field in the "Samplings Setting" tab, offering greater
flexibility.
2. Rule Scope & Filters ("Settings" Tab)
Rules can be scoped to apply only under specific conditions via filters.
• General Tab: Apply broad filters using:
o Item Family
o Supplier Family
o The rule will only trigger for items belonging to the selected
categories.
• Additional Tab: Apply precise filters based on defined values related to:
o Stock attributes
o Order headers and lines
o Article/item master data
o Various Third Parties (e.g., specific suppliers, carriers) defined in
SpeedWMS.
Sensitivity: Internal

3. Sampling Logic Configuration ("Sampling Setting" Tab)
This tab defines when and how sampling occurs.
• A. Trigger Method: Defines the event that initiates sampling.
o Free: User enters a custom query.
o Standard: User selects from system-defined triggers:
▪ Rupture: Defines a specific moment (e.g., time-based) to start
sampling.
▪ New Item: When an item unknown in the system enters stock.
▪ New Item in Reception: When a new item is received into the
environment.
▪ New Traceability Information: When a new traceability element
(e.g., batch, serial) is detected on an item.
▪ Full Support: At any change of the handling unit/load carrier
(e.g., pallet).
• B. Sampling Parameters: Defines the details of the sample.
o Quality: The quality status/grade of the sample to be taken for control.
o Location: The destination location where the sample should be
deposited for inspection.
o Quantity: The amount to sample. Two methods exist:
1. Value: A fixed quantity is defined by the user in a dedicated
field, based on a selected Stock Unit (SU).
▪ Important: When using a fixed value, ensure the
items being sampled actually manage the selected
Stock Unit in their master data.
2. Percentage: A user-defined percentage of the total received
quantity will be sampled. The sampled quantity therefore
scales with the receipt size.
Sensitivity: Internal

Resolving Missing Weights on GDNs / Picklists (Commodities – Durban)
1. Background
Missing weights typically occur when:
1. An order is validated and then brought back to Seizure status:
o Weights are initially stored in REL_DAT and inherited by STK_DAT.
o When stock leaves the system, this information is cleared from
STK_DAT.
o Returning stock does not automatically repopulate STK_DAT.
2. During reception, weight information may not have been correctly inherited
into STK_DAT.
2. Step-by-Step Resolution
Step 1 – Check the Order Status
Ensure the order is editable (not validated):
SELECT *
FROM ope_dat
WHERE ope_nooe = 'order_number'
AND act_code = 'zar';
Step 2 – Check Missions Linked to the Order
Review all missions associated with the order:
SELECT *
FROM mil_dat
WHERE ope_nooe = 'order_number'
AND act_code = 'zar';
Note: Some supports may already be validated (picked); only unvalidated supports
can be updated.
Sensitivity: Internal

metadata.source: Speed WMS – GDN  Picklist Weight Resolution (Durban Commodities).txt
metadata.source_file: Speed WMS – GDN  Picklist Weight Resolution (Durban Commodities).txt

text:
Step 3 – Update Valid Supports
Copy the weight data from REL_DAT to STK_DAT. Replace 'support_number_1',
'support_number_2', ... with the actual support numbers from MIL_DAT:
UPDATE s
SET
s.stk_num13 = r.rel_num13,
s.stk_num15 = r.rel_num14,
s.stk_num16 = r.rel_num15,
s.stk_num17 = r.rel_num15
FROM stk_dat s
JOIN rel_dat r
ON s.stk_nosu = r.rel_nosu
AND s.act_code = r.act_code
WHERE s.stk_nosu IN ('support_number_1', 'support_number_2', ...)
AND s.act_code = 'zar';
Step 4 – Verify the Fix
• Print the GDN / Picklist.
• If weights now appear correctly, no further action is needed.
Step 5 – If Weights Still Don’t Show
1. Go back to MIL_DAT.
2. Unvalidate all lines that were already picked.
3. Rerun the update query from Step 3.
4. Print the GDN / Picklist again to confirm weights are correctly displayed.
Notes
• Only update unvalidated supports to avoid inconsistencies.
Sensitivity: Internal

Handling Loaded Support Tickets (Loading Management)
Sensitivity: Internal
System: Speed WMS
Module: Loading Management
Audience: Support / Technical Team
Purpose
This procedure is used when a support ticket indicates that containers are already
loaded, but the Loading Management Line table (CHL_DAT) is not correctly updated.
Important:
These steps should be executed only if the system does not update automatically.
Step 1: Create Temporary Order Table (#order_table)
This step creates a temporary table to capture order numbers linked to loaded
containers for further processing.
SELECT DISTINCT
chg.chg_lib,
chl.ope_nooe,
chg.act_code
INTO #order_table
FROM chg_dat chg
JOIN chl_dat chl
ON chg.chg_code = chl.chg_code
AND chg.chg_date = chl.chg_date
WHERE chg.act_code = 'ZAR';
Outcome:

Sensitivity: Internal
System: Speed WMS
Module Impacted: Manifest / ETAT
Audience: Support / Technical Team
Issue Description
Operations reported that some LPNs do not appear on the manifest.
Investigation shows that in certain cases:
• LPN data from MIL_DAT does not fully pass into SEX_DAT
• The affected record in SEX_DAT has a missing order number:
o SEX_NOOE = 0
• Since the manifest ETAT relies on SEX_DAT, the LPN does not display on the
manifest
The root cause is currently unknown.
The steps below provide a temporary fix when the issue occurs.
How to Identify Affected LPNs
Run the following query to find LPNs where the order number is missing:
SELECT
sex.SEX_SUPE,
mil.MIL_SUPP,
mil.OPE_NOOE,
mil.MIE_NOMI,
sex.SEX_NOMI,
sex.SEX_NOOE
FROM SEX_DAT sex
JOIN MIL_DAT mil
ON mil.ACT_CODE = sex.SEX_ACT

Procedure: Resolving Serial Number Issues in Speed (e.g., INC0379425)
1. Objective
To resolve incidents where serial numbers are not associating correctly in Speed,
even though they appear in reports (e.g., SSRS), using database verification and
updates.
2. Example Incident
Incident: INC0379425 – Skyworth Durban
Issue:
• 100 serial numbers for 2 pallets (PSD000977 and PSD000984) were not
associating in Speed.
• Serial numbers appeared correctly in the SSRS serial number report, but not in
Speed.
Root Cause:
• Spaces or special characters (e.g., line breaks) were present in the serial number
table (NSE_DAT).
• Speed does not accept special characters in serial number fields.
3. Steps to Resolve
Step 1 – Verify Data in Database
Check serial number records in the production Speed database:
SELECT NSE_SSCCC, *
FROM nse_dat
WHERE NSE_SSCCC LIKE '%PSD000984%';
• nse_dat: Serial number table
• NSE_SSCCC: Field representing pallet number
Step 2 – Identify the Issue
Sensitivity: Internal

metadata.source: Speed WMS – Serial Number Issue Resolution Procedure.txt
metadata.source_file: Speed WMS – Serial Number Issue Resolution Procedure.txt

text:
• Look for spaces, line breaks, or special characters in the NSE_SSCCC field.
• Confirm the affected records correspond to the incident pallets.
Step 3 – Fix the Issue
Remove unwanted characters using the REPLACE function:
UPDATE nse_dat
SET NSE_SSCCC = REPLACE(NSE_SSCCC, CHAR(10), '')
WHERE act_code = 'RSADBNWH'
AND art_code IN ('SKY-HS6409', 'SKY-R012000030', 'SKY-R012000029');
• CHAR(10) represents a line break or special character
• Filter by ACT_CODE and ART_CODE to update only relevant records
Step 4 – Validate the Fix
1. Re-run the SELECT query from Step 1 to confirm that special characters are
removed.
2. Check with operations that the serial numbers now associate correctly in
Speed.
4. Notes
• Always verify the data before applying updates to avoid impacting unrelated
records.
• Maintain an audit log of:
o Pallet/serial numbers updated
o Database changes made
o Date/time and operator
• This procedure can be reused for any serial number issue caused by unwanted
characters.
Sensitivity: Internal

metadata.source: Speed WMS – Serial Number Issue Resolution Procedure.txt
metadata.source_file: Speed WMS – Serial Number Issue Resolution Procedure.txt

Handling Issues with Unknown Supports
Sensitivity: Internal
System: Speed WMS
Audience: Support / Technical Team
Purpose
This procedure is used when an order encounters unknown support issues,
typically caused by support numbers not being correctly validated or loaded.
Step 1: Check Mission Details in Speed
1. Navigate to Preparation Module → Manage Missions.
2. Open the Validated tab.
3. Filter the list to locate the affected mission.
4. Double-click the mission to open the mission details.
Step 2: Verify Support Numbers
• Confirm that both support numbers are visible:
o iLPN
o 0LPN
• If both supports are present, proceed to database verification.
Step 3: Check Support Status in the Database
Use the following query to identify supports that are still in status 020:
SELECT *
FROM SEX_DAT
WHERE SEX_STSUP = '020'
AND SEX_NOOE = 'order number'
AND SEX_ACT = 'ZAR';
Sensitivity: Internal

metadata.source: Speed WMS – Unknown Support Issue Resolution Procedure.txt
metadata.source_file: Speed WMS – Unknown Support Issue Resolution Procedure.txt

text:
Step 4: Identify the Issue
• Supports with status 020 indicate that they are not yet validated
• These supports must be updated before containers can be loaded
Step 5: Update Support Status to Validated
If support numbers are found with status 020, update them to 040:
UPDATE SEX_DAT
SET SEX_STSUP = '040'
WHERE SEX_STSUP = '020'
AND SEX_NOOE = 'order number'
AND SEX_ACT = 'ZAR';
Step 6: Request Container Loading
• Once the update is complete, notify the Operations team
• Operations can now load the containers successfully
Expected Outcome
• Support numbers are validated (040)
• Unknown support issue is resolved
• Containers can be loaded without errors
Important Notes
• This procedure requires database access and must be executed by Support
• Always verify support visibility in iLPN and 0LPN before updating the
database
• Ensure the correct order number and activity code are used
Sensitivity: Internal

Please be advised that there is a known and pending issue affecting ZAR
commodities, where missions can be loaded even when the full order has not been
completely picked.
This behaviour is currently causing operational backlogs and delays.
Current Status
• The issue has been formally escalated to BKS.
• We are awaiting their feedback and a permanent fix.
Temporary Mitigation
While waiting for BKS resolution, a temporary workaround has been implemented:
• A task scheduler runs every 5 minutes to update affected missions.

This is a temporary solution and should be treated as such.

sex.sex_stsup

Clarins Mission Line Validation – Internal Support Procedure
Sensitivity: Internal
Audience: Support / Technical Team
System: Speed WMS
Purpose
This procedure is used to correct and validate mission lines for Clarins orders when:
• Orders are not validating correctly
• Mission lines are stuck below validation status
• Mission lines are not linked to valid stock locations
Validation must be performed only using active picking locations and open-box
stock, not reserve or full-carton stock.
Key Parameters
Before running the script, define the following:
DECLARE @ArtCode varchar(50) = '80110136'; -- SKU / Article Code
DECLARE @Stk_Keyu int = 218923; -- Selected Stock Key
Step 1: Identify Orders and Mission Lines Not Yet Validated
This step identifies:
• Orders with mission lines already in status 040
• Orders whose overall status is below 040
• Mission lines below validation status for the specified SKU
WITH ope_mil_040 AS (
SELECT
OPE_KEYU,
ACT_CODE,
OPE_NOOE,
OPE_STAT,
Sensitivity: Internal

OPE_DAT.OPE_NoVA,
(
SELECT COUNT(MIL_KEYU)
FROM MIL_DAT
WHERE MIL_DAT.OPE_NoOE = OPE_DAT.OPE_NoOE
AND MIL_DAT.ACT_CODE = OPE_DAT.ACT_CODE
AND MIL_STAT = '040'
) AS MIL_040,
(
SELECT COUNT(MIL_KEYU)
FROM MIL_DAT
WHERE MIL_DAT.OPE_NoOE = OPE_DAT.OPE_NoOE
AND MIL_DAT.ACT_CODE = OPE_DAT.ACT_CODE
) AS Nb_MIL
FROM OPE_DAT
WHERE ACT_CODE = 'RSAJHBCLA'
)
SELECT
O.OPE_KEYU,
O.ACT_CODE,
O.OPE_NoOE,
O.OPE_STAT,
MIL_040,
Nb_MIL,
M.MIL_KEYU,
M.MIL_STAT,
M.ACT_CODE,
Sensitivity: Internal

M.ART_CODE,
M.MIL_QTTA,
M.MIL_EMP,
M.MIL_NoSU,
M.MIL_SUPP,
M.MIL_LOT1P,
M.MIL_DLUOP
FROM ope_mil_040 O
JOIN MIL_DAT M
ON O.ACT_CODE = M.ACT_CODE
AND O.OPE_NoOE = M.OPE_NoOE
WHERE MIL_040 > 0
AND O.OPE_STAT < '040'
AND M.MIL_STAT < '040'
AND M.ART_CODE = @ArtCode
ORDER BY M.MIL_STAT, Nb_MIL;
Step 2: Identify Valid Stock for Validation
This step finds active stock locations for the SKU that:
• Are in Inspection (INS) status
• Are located in picking zones
• Are actively being consumed (open boxes)
SELECT
STK_KEYU,
STK_LIEU,
ART_CODE,
STK_QTE,
QUA_CODE,
Sensitivity: Internal

STK_NoSU,
STK_LOT1,
STK_DLUO,
(
SELECT SUM(MIL_QTTP)
FROM MIL_DAT
WHERE MIL_DAT.ACT_CODE = STK_DAT.ACT_CODE
AND MIL_DAT.QUA_CODE = 'INS'
AND MIL_DAT.ART_CODE = STK_DAT.ART_CODE
AND MIL_DAT.MIL_EMP = STK_DAT.STK_LIEU
AND MIL_STAT < '040'
) AS MIL_QTTP
FROM STK_DAT
WHERE ACT_CODE = 'RSAJHBCLA'
AND QUA_CODE = 'INS'
AND ART_CODE = @ArtCode
AND STK_LIEU IN (
SELECT EMP_LIEU
FROM EMZ_BAS
WHERE ZEM_CODE = 'CLA_PIC'
)
ORDER BY ART_CODE, STK_LIEU, STK_NoSU;
Step 3: Reassign Mission Lines to Valid Stock Location
This step updates mission lines that:
• Are in status 020
• Are not currently linked to valid stock
• Match the specified SKU
Sensitivity: Internal

Only up to 150 mission lines are updated at a time.
BEGIN TRAN
UPDATE MIL_DAT
SET MIL_EMP = s.STK_LIEU
FROM (
SELECT STK_LIEU, STK_NoSU, STK_LOT1, STK_DLUO
FROM STK_DAT
WHERE STK_KEYU = @Stk_Keyu
AND ART_CODE = @ArtCode
) s
WHERE MIL_STAT < '040'
AND MIL_KEYU IN (
SELECT TOP 150 M.MIL_KEYU
FROM MIL_DAT M
LEFT JOIN STK_DAT S
ON M.ACT_CODE = S.ACT_CODE
AND M.ART_CODE = S.ART_CODE
AND M.MIL_EMP = S.STK_LIEU
AND M.MIL_NoSU = S.STK_NoSU
WHERE M.ACT_CODE = 'RSAJHBCLA'
AND M.MIL_STAT = '020'
AND S.STK_KEYU IS NULL
AND M.ART_CODE = @ArtCode
)
COMMIT TRAN
Sensitivity: Internal

Critical Business Rules (Must Be Followed)
Stock Selection Rules
• Only Active Picking Locations
• Do NOT use Reserve Locations
• Do NOT use Full Cartons
• Only Open-Box Stock
How to Identify Open-Box Stock
• If multiple LPNs for the same SKU have identical quantities, these represent full
cartons → Do not use
• If an LPN shows quantity being reduced, it represents an open box → Valid for
validation
Important Notes
• Validation from reserve stock must be handled via the replenishment process
• This script is intended for Support use only
• Always verify stock behavior before assigning STK_KEYU
Sensitivity: Internal

Clarins Shortfall Order – Mission Location Update Procedure
Sensitivity: Internal
Client: Clarins
System: Speed WMS
Audience: Support / Technical Team
Purpose
This procedure is used when a Clarins order has been launched and results in a
shortfall, even though:
• The SKU or LPN is confirmed to be in stock, and
• The order line is missing a valid picking location at launch time.
In this scenario, the mission must be manually updated to assign the correct
picking location.
Preconditions
Before modifying any mission lines, verify the following:
• The SKU exists in stock
• The LPN exists and is available
• The stock is located in a valid active picking location
• The mission line has a status below 040
Step 1: Identify Affected Mission Lines
Retrieve all mission lines for the affected SKU that are not yet validated.
SELECT MIL_KEYU, MIL_EMP, *
FROM MIL_DAT
WHERE ART_CODE = '80110136'
AND MIL_STAT < '040';
Confirm that the order you are working on appears in the result set.
Sensitivity: Internal

Step 2: Determine the Correct Picking Location
• Identify the correct stock location (STK_LIEU) from which the SKU should be
picked
• Copy the MIL_KEYU(s) associated with the affected order line(s)
• Copy the target picking location
Step 3: Update the Mission Line Picking Location
Assign the correct picking location to the mission line.
UPDATE MIL_DAT
SET MIL_EMP = 'CA002A035',
MIL_EMPO = 'CA002A035'
WHERE MIL_KEYU IN (144522, 147153);
Expected Outcome
• The mission line is now linked to a valid picking location
• The shortfall condition is resolved
• The order can proceed through validation and picking
Important Notes
• This procedure applies only to Clarins
• Mission lines must have MIL_STAT < '040'
• Updates must be performed by Support, due to database access restrictions
• Always validate stock availability before modifying missions
Sensitivity: Internal

How to Cancel an Order That Has Already Been Shipped
Overview
Once an order has been shipped, it is assigned status 070.
Orders in status 070 cannot be cancelled or deleted directly in the Speed system.
To cancel such an order, it must first be reverted to an earlier status (060).
This reversal must be performed directly in the database and can only be done by
the Support team, as they have the required database access.
Step 1: Verify the Order in the Database
Confirm the order details and current status before making any changes.
SELECT OPE_KEYU, OPE_NOOE, *
FROM OPE_DAT
WHERE ACT_CODE = 'Activity Account'
AND OPE_NOOE = [Order Number];
Step 2: Revert the Order Status from 070 to 060
Update the order status in the database to allow further processing in Speed.
UPDATE OPE_DAT
SET OPE_STAT = '060'
WHERE ACT_CODE = 'Activity Account'
AND OPE_NOOE = [Order Number]
AND OPE_KEYU = [Order Keyu];
Important:
This update must be executed by the Support team, as end users do not have database
access.
Step 3: Invalidate Mission Lines in Speed
After the order status has been reverted to 060, continue in the Speed application:
1. Navigate to the Mission tab.
Sensitivity: Internal

2. Select the relevant Mission.
3. The Mission Header page will open, showing mission metadata.
4. Double-click the mission header to display the Mission Lines.
5. Invalidate all mission lines.
6. If the order has multiple mission headers, repeat this process for each one.
Step 4: Cancel the Mission
• Once all mission lines are invalidated, the order will automatically move to
status 030.
• From status 030, cancel the mission.
• After mission cancellation, the order will move to status 010.
Step 5: Cancel the Order
• When the order reaches status 010, it can now be fully cancelled in the system.
Key Notes for RAG Usage
• Orders in status 070 cannot be cancelled directly
• Status 070 → 060 requires a database update
• Only Support can perform database updates
• All mission lines must be invalidated before mission cancellation
• Final order cancellation is only possible at status 010
Sensitivity: Internal

Troubleshooting and Configuring Printer Options
Author: Micah Samuel
Introduction
This guide provides step-by-step instructions for uninstalling, importing, and
configuring a printer using Printix and Windows settings.
Steps
1. Uninstall the Printer
• Ensure the printer is removed if it is already installed.
• Go to Windows Settings → Printers & Scanners.
• Select the printer to uninstall.
• Click Remove device.
2. Import the Printer from Printix
• Open the Tungsten Printix Client.
• Search for the printer (e.g., ovl).
• Select the desired printer (e.g., OVL ZA012-OVL-MSCBL-00-BW).
• Click Add to import the printer.
3. Access Printer Settings
• Open Windows Settings.
• Search for Printers & Scanners.
• Select Printers & scanners from the search results.
4. Select and Configure the Printer
• From the list of printers, select the printer you want to configure (e.g., ZA012OVL-MSCBL-00-BW).
• Click Printing preferences.
Sensitivity: Internal

5. Configure Print Options
• In the pop-up window, select Print Options.
• From the Printing Mode dropdown menu, select Direct Thermal.
• Click Apply.
• Click OK to save changes.
Figures
• Figure 1: Printer selection in Windows Settings
• Figure 2: Printers & Scanners search
• Figure 3: Select printer from list
• Figure 4: Printing preferences window
• Figure 5: Print Options configuration
Tips:
• Always remove old printer instances before importing a new one.
• Confirm the Printing Mode matches the printer type (e.g., thermal vs. inkjet).
• Apply and test print to ensure correct configuration.

Updating Expiry Dates for Clarins Products
Sensitivity: Internal
Client: Clarins
System: Speed WMS
Audience: Support / Technical Team
1. Objective
To update expiry dates for Clarins products in the WMS database, ensuring consistency
between:
• Stock records (STK_DAT)
• Picking / mission records (MIL_DAT)
2. Procedure
Step 1: Verify the Stock Record
Confirm that the LPN exists and review the current expiry date.
SELECT stk_dluo, *
FROM stk_dat
WHERE stk_nosu = 'LPN No'
AND act_code = 'RSAJHBCLA';
✔ Proceed only if the record exists.
Step 2: Update the Stock Table (STK_DAT)
Update the expiry date to the new value provided.
UPDATE stk_dat
SET stk_dluo = 'New Date'
WHERE stk_nosu = 'LPN No'
AND act_code = 'RSAJHBCLA';
Ensure the date format matches the system standard (e.g. YYYY-MM-DD).
Sensitivity: Internal

Determine whether the LPN is involved in any open missions.
SELECT mil_dluop, *
FROM mil_dat
WHERE mil_nosu = 'LPN No'
AND act_code = 'RSAJHBCLA'
AND mil_stat < '040';
Step 4: Update the Picking Table (If Required)
If Step 3 returns records, update the expiry date in the picking table.
UPDATE mil_dat
SET mil_dluop = 'New Date'
WHERE mil_nosu = 'LPN No'
AND act_code = 'RSAJHBCLA'
AND mil_stat < '040';
3. Important Notes
• Always update STK_DAT first, then MIL_DAT if applicable
• If no records are found in MIL_DAT, no update is required
• Keep an audit record of:
o LPN
o Old expiry date
o New expiry date
• Perform updates in Test / QA before Production (where applicable)

DOCUMENT: Speed WMS Inbound Data Model — Attendus & Réceptions — SAFETY RULES

  1. Always filter by ACT_CODE on every table access
  2. Do NOT join REL_DAT directly to REA_DAT unless the expected receipt has exactly 1 reception line — use MVT_DAT as the bridge instead
  3. Stock creation movement TMV_CODE = 10010 must be used to correctly identify inbound stock movements
  4. REA_CTAF in REA_DAT is the equivalent of TIE_CODE — this is a named exception to the standard field naming rule
  5. Always execute SELECT before any UPDATE or DELETE operations
  6. Do not execute UPDATE in production without approval

  2. NEVER join MIE_DAT with OPE_DAT or CHL_DAT using order number directly — route through MIL_DAT instead
  3. Loading header composite key: ACT_CODE + CHG_CODE + CHG_DATE
  4. Loading line composite key: ACT_CODE + CHG_CODE + CHG_DATE + OPE_NOOE
  5. Stock definitive exit: TMV_CODE = 40010 or 40110
  6. SEX_DAT uses SEX_ACT not ACT_CODE — always check this when joining to SEX_DAT
  7. Always execute SELECT before UPDATE operations
  8. Do not execute UPDATE in production without approval
  9. Support-level SQL only

SpeedWMS – Deadline Reservation
Access
• Menu: Stock / Deadline Reservation
Purpose
• Analyzes reserved stock to ensure that reservations are up-to-date.
• Automatically removes reservations for all stock items whose reservation
date is earlier than the current date.
Notes
• Works in conjunction with the reservation setup at the item level (Unit
modification section of the Item).
• Helps prevent outdated reservations from blocking stock availability.
Sensitivity: Internal

SpeedWMS – Quality Assignment
Access
• Menu: Stock / Quality allocation
Purpose
• Applies quality rules to stock items according to the configurations defined
in the environment.
• Ensures that stock in the warehouse is assigned the correct quality status
based on pre-configured rules.
Notes
• The quality rules are defined at the item level in the settings.
• This process helps maintain consistency in stock quality and prevents
misallocation during picking or replenishment.
Sensitivity: Internal

SpeedWMS – View Stocks
Access
• Menu: Stock / Stock
Purpose
• Provides a comprehensive overview of stock declared in the SpeedWMS
environment.
• Enables monitoring, analysis, and certain operations depending on the tab.
Tabs & Functionality
Tab Purpose / Notes
Total stocks by reference and by quality. No operations can be
Stock
performed here.
Batch Total stocks by reference and by batch. No operations possible.
Detailed view by medium, location, etc. All stock operations are
Details
performed from this tab.
Movements History of all stock movements recorded in SpeedWMS.
Expected Displays the list of registered expected items.
Manufacturing In progress.
In seizure In progress.
To be
Planned stocks assigned to orders launched in preparation.
prepared
Taken Stocks whose mission lines have been picked.
Prepared Stocks whose mission lines have been validated.
In expedition Stocks linked to an order awaiting shipment.
Shipped Stocks linked to an order that has already been shipped.
Filters
Sensitivity: Internal

• Direct filters at the top: article, supplier, or product family (classification).
• Advanced filter function allows searching by additional criteria beyond
default filters.
Sensitivity: Internal

Automatic Search Location – Assigning Planned Locations Automatically
Purpose:
• Automatically determine a planned location for each receipt line, instead of
assigning it manually.
• Optimizes storage placement based on predefined rules.
Steps
1. Select the receipt lines for which you want to perform the automatic search.
2. Either:
o Right-click → Launch automatic search, or
o Click the Location search button at the bottom-right of the window.
System Behavior
• SpeedWMS proposes the most optimized storage location for each support
based on the criteria of the automatic search rule:
o Zone type
o Stock constraints
o Item characteristics
o Capacity limitations
• If the system cannot find a suitable location for a line (e.g., storage zone full,
criteria not met), the “Search completed” box remains unchecked.
Key Point:
Automatic search saves time and ensures consistency but may require manual
intervention for lines where no suitable location is found.
Sensitivity: Internal

Declarative Storage – Assigning Planned Locations
Access:
• Open a Reception form → Use the Assign option from the popup/context
menu.
Purpose
• Assign a destination location for each support manually.
• Supports can then be prepared for storage movements and later used for
order picking.
Steps
1. Open the reception form.
2. Select a line (support) → choose Assign from the contextual menu.
3. Fill in the Planned location field for each support:
o Enter the location name manually, or
o Search and select via the Assign the planned location option.
Outcome
• As soon as a destination location is assigned, the support’s status changes
to 03 (“movement to be performed”).
• This indicates the support has a known planned location and is ready for
storage processing.
Sensitivity: Internal

Storage tab
All the generated reception lines will be accessible via the menu Receiving / Receipts,
then in the Storage tab of the receipt:
The following will be specified in particular for each support entered:
.Its current location, which matches the location of the reception
.The reference picking layout for the item
.The intended location of destination, blank by default in administrative mode
.The status of the support, depending on the status of the activity
The ranking will be done either declaratively or through the use of parameterized
location search rules.
Note that it will be possible to store the goods directly on their picking location. The
button Initialize picking will allow you to directly enter the picking location as the
destination location of the selected lines.
Whichever method is chosen, the result will be the same: it is a question of obtaining a
planned location for each line of the reception.
Sensitivity: Internal

Storage Validation
Access:
• Storage tab of the receipt.
• Select the lines to be stored.
• Click Validate Storage (button at the bottom or via the contextual menu).
What Happens During Storage Validation
1. The system moves the selected media (pallets, bins, etc.) to their planned
location automatically.
2. The status of the support is updated to:
o 01 – Support in place
o This indicates the media is now stored and available for order
preparation.
3. Information for each line is updated in the system after processing.
Key Points:
• Storage validation finalizes the placement of media in the warehouse.
• Only validated media (status 01) can be used for further operations like order
picking or preparation.
Sensitivity: Internal

SpeedWMS – Status of a Support
When stock is generated during reception, each storage support (e.g., pallet, bin) is
assigned a status depending on its handling and location assignment.
Initial Status After Reception
1. 01 – Support in place
o Support is already in its location.
o Typically used when locations are not managed.
2. 02 – Location to be assigned
o Support is on the reception platform.
o Destination location is unknown at this stage.
Assigned Location
• When a destination location is assigned (manually in the Storage tab or via
automatic location search), the support status changes to:
3. 03 – Movement to be performed
o Support knows its planned storage location, but has not yet been
moved.
After Movement
• Once the support is moved to the planned location:
o Status changes from 03 → 01
o Initial location is replaced with the planned location.
o The movement is recorded in Speed history.
Key Notes:
• Status 01 can represent both “already in place” and “moved to its
destination.”
• Status 02 is temporary until the system or user assigns a location.
Sensitivity: Internal
